body.title: Hill repeats Tempo
body.body:
![IMG_1054.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/23ywuibYKXKSK29Z4jPJWtxFku3H29yWMJVW5288m2Ss8qHEGTRDrorC8r42CGGaoAZ4D.jpeg)

![IMG_1069.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/23swkNnbakFjNPeJYRpBeDU1FJEPProdqNRKcVgZnND7ZP4MrBbZza8x8QhDVcp4ZUsgp.jpeg)

I had a spare hour to run in between appointments. As my planned hill session for Wednesday would be making my schedule to tight, I decided to go for the hill work today. 

When I got to the hill it started raining quite a bit making me pretty underdressed. Luckely I was wearing a cap so I would not get the rain in my face. I decided to make it a stronger effort than planned. Instead of doing a technical session, I went for some tempo work in the sets, not all out but a considerable faster pace compared to last Sunday. 


![IMG_1065.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/23wg917Sn7ZEAyLDYzDtPT9XGjJChZRsNCA7h1Fz9HWPWmDwKkN5xYGxkmw6drTqNRPcY.jpeg)

![IMG_1066.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/EoCap6aYR94mR7ojMWCEYexpXgg86o8Nbcq5uYd2LxnfKUyAVXRBwgfNDQvf72YPHLi.jpeg)

Doing so felt good, it kept me warm and the tempo got used very quick. After 10 minutes I wasn’t even bothered with the rain anymore. 

![IMG_1057.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/23xp8Z1STgyAkCk46A5s5r8WKTpf6Gs61KisP7wzX5LJwg31ngUtRZK1aYtJ9NEdqbcub.jpeg)

![IMG_1055.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rainbowdash4l/23y8sbB1cYqQ2E2rpf8oMqQTE2wCtDVAPw9vGPNHjxqNAxJd23cFAWWy4hk8qcwi2CXHd.jpeg)

While I did took nutrition with me, I opted to stick to just drinking some electrolytes and ignore the energy gels for now. The run was short enough to just work through without any issues. 

Whereas I normally run with my music on, I decided to run without today - mostly as this is something I also need to train for the Jungfrau Marathon as I will be running alongside a friend - so curious how I will experience that as it felt very easy to just create your own bubble with music , put your game mode on and keep out all distractions. Going to be fun! 

Happy Running!

body.body:
[![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUSiHMqodZbxRSfRBPch7YAN3EMq9UiAvLdViSLy54Xfe/260840b686a13423f947bed939a20c3e)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=efootjoker-yt/ace348f8)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=efootjoker-yt/ace348f8)


---

---

<center>**Hello everyone and welcome back to my blog.**</center>

---
#
As Lord Shimura and I continued, we reached the Old Togo Rice Fields. Once it was a rice field, but now it was hard to tell. All around was scorched land, blackened rice, and a burning smell. The Mongols had set the entire field on fire. Lord Shimura became very angry when he saw this scene.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXwEcLXLpMa4nz9RN7Xcy9pHM5r7Xo9m7S7zL1N6ftz83/snapshot.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXJbyPSXWCa4AScWBiMNzWLvZ8BYDtU5sLetrLVjA6Qkf/snapshot_3.png)

After a while, we saw a patrol of Mongols moving there. As soon as Lord Shimura saw them, he rushed towards them in anger. I also joined the battle from behind. The enemies sensed our presence and started attacking. I used a smoke bomb first. The smoke threw them off balance, and at that opportunity, I killed three soldiers with the Chain Assassin skill.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYTiYVg9xKKepboWb2uqGTVrdA87ccfiRws6dWRf7VrSL/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS7NszXf8turCag7AvKRSsNpFrs12SxMno9rft1Az4xA1/snapshot_5.png)

One of the soldiers was an archer. Archers are very dangerous, so I spotted him first. I got close and killed him. The rest of the soldiers were fighting Lord Shimura. I quickly went forward to help him and finished off all the enemies one by one.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfNBmuKQJgrtvkExGVPVdM6NLbcuyUd2f7tgbe1vhKGw3/snapshot_6.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSoAFGikqUAEPcbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y/snapshot_7.png)

This fight was really enjoyable. Because there were different types of soldiers here. Some with swords, some with bows, and some with spears. So I had to use different stances to fight each enemy. It was quite an interesting experience to fight by changing stances repeatedly.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ7i6i8Rwst4s8QDRMKSazxGz5YhUE7zydhS5ijvx8agg/snapshot_8.png)

After all the soldiers were dead, Lord Shimura again praised my fighting skills. Then we moved on to another fort ahead. That fort was called Fort Ito, which was then completely occupied by the Mongols.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUpL4HCkyHSxbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y/snapshot_9.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWmd2zTiyq7R69CHPaQvpjwAvZX8uZm3mWvRGYGrehuHW/snapshot_10.png)

We quickly killed the two guards in front of the fort. But before they died, they alerted the soldiers inside. As a result, the gate opened and a few more soldiers came out.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRLJuNgUPMfbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y/snapshot_11.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRpDaxWBnbQtLSYLMbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y/snapshot_12.png)

One of them was a little different. He had some kind of explosive bomb in his hand. He was throwing bombs at us repeatedly. When the bomb exploded, it caused a lot of damage. So I targeted him first and killed him quickly. Then I finished off the rest of the soldiers one by one.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRHWMN2fEJgEGqHWkCFwHUXguQb58YmbUCEdCTeNXho99/snapshot_13.png)

I saw the soldiers inside the castle shooting fireworks into the sky. Lord Shimura understood this as a signal for help. If they were not stopped quickly, more soldiers would come. So I quickly entered the castle.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY7zq5pfarbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y/snapshot_14.png)

As I entered, I realized that the situation was difficult. About 20-25 soldiers surrounded me. I made a big mistake here. I did not use any ghost weapons and did not give importance to the archers. As a result, four or five archers started shooting arrows at once, and a soldier with a gun was firing explosive bullets. I lost the battle for the first time.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme5wcPBkcm9eRefeYegaoM2tiMZX93emUEXZkx1ESseLM/snapshot_15.png)

But I didn't make that mistake the second time. This time, I entered and used the kunai to throw the soldiers off balance.  I killed the gunner soldier first. I found all the archers one by one and killed them.

Lord Shimura also entered and started fighting with the other soldiers. After finishing off the archers, I went to help him. After a long and hard fight, we were able to kill all the Mongol soldiers.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZox7qbc1q5mlw63yd2u2cn0hs6jnzf2gljhr486u3dkgm2y6oHz/snapshot_16.png)

body.title: MY EXPERIENCE WITH CAMPUS LIFE
body.body:
Hello everyone your welcome to my blog today.

Stepping into the university I was very happy because I stayed at home for a year and it was such an exciting moment for me when I heard that I got admission. I got admission into Abia state university Uturu the year 2018 October.





![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYsHDkJouifUxZ5d7BvswG6wNvNQ4A5iYW2Dju93rAXrG/1773140314223.jpg)


I was already running late as I got admitted late and paying all the requirements needed took up so much of my time, but indeed it was a good experience because I got to meet new people who helped me navigate my way through as a year one student before getting my accommodation and fully settling into students’ life.

My normal routine for waking up at 5am every morning so the same was applicable to school. When I wake up, I go down to the hostels tap to fetch water and refill my cans and then prepare what I will eat for the day, then I move on to getting the clothes I want to wear to school ready.
Then I would move on to having my bath and brushing, then I dish my food and eat then pack my bags and step out for lectures.

Coming down to how my daily routine can be sometimes, well on a good day it can go well and on some bad days it can be very stressful and messy. Sometimes lectures can be all packed up in a day and when you leave your hostel early in the morning you come back being so stressed and tired that most times you end up being irritated at the end of the day.

My lecture starts most times by 9am most of the times and it lasts till 4 or 5pm. But sometimes it starts by 6:30am, you can imagine, we had this lecturer that lectured us on computer, and he lived around the school so he would always come to school by 6:30am and if he doesn’t see you in class then he would take his attendance and keep the latecomers outside the class.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX6nicFKQ6xdPGUxAt8nCWpfzsbszjRCRbE9Dy9SRJkqB/1773140342903.jpg)





My favorite spot in school was the school cafeteria I go there almost every day because it has a lobby that is always cool to stay in in go there with my friends to study most of the time and charge our phones during the day because we might not have light in the hostels.

Then during evening periods, I go for my church activities or go for drama rehearsals, most times it runs from 5pm to 6pm, after which I return home to have dinner, shower and relax for a new day.


A big shout out goes to hive the students’ community for this weekly prompt to share my experience as a student. It’s my pleasure sharing my experience with everyone.

Thank you for stopping by my blog

body.body:
![Blue and Yellow Professional Webinar Youtube Thumbnail (40).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23wWwEKRieu9jamMZXu2y5aKmeeJES7MeiAG31w8Vpcd5t6LNQ7Ed498Pk9yaTB7kaSSX.png) ***
![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHA37mQtCuynkak9C9VAyTtPNZ193z3v9HzUXNRYfNBKpop4B452wXWGAr95ns7Froa3QYr2tHe7aDsDXTJuz6E8PeAV3edWS3NGxHQJHC9xJn9eUpGW.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23uEz3qUu1cpWPYjmp2LnK1i4RcXoAhocX2Rzpq9uYyMScovNm77MZBozX7i1NM59BnSf.png) Oh yeah, I’ve had to learn a few new things as well. Yeah, it’s not been easy, but when certain things in your life have been going only in a particular direction, it’s usually a good idea to take a step back and reconsider some of the things you’re doing. Because, as they say, insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result. This is why I’m being intentional about the things I wish to change. Sometimes, it’s not really about learning a new skill or reading a new book. Many times, we say that no knowledge is a waste, but there are periods when I don’t even vibe with that saying at all. Because any knowledge that you don’t make use of has to be a waste, right? What’s the point of learning a skill or reading a book if you won’t do the things the book asks you to, or if you won’t actually use the skill to make your life better? ![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHA37mQtCuynkak9C9VAxm3nacdB7gLmLiZLuYVhHeNsRgxL6WKJoam3hs2B7ZLAp2jwaLFEwoAbLKzAfpv2DhtyvHbJunTbU58RMbxtkvefNK4qj8EA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23uQkLUmr2XGp8UpLcdtKeQrWDNnK5jemLpyFynqgRKtzZaqtByEwcX3DoUEyB8Pwi9DN.png) Well, for me, I’ve always been quite proactive. When I learn a skill, I follow through with it. I didn’t learn writing, but that led me to other various skills that I learned during the course of my writing career. I became a certified Book Project Consultant and also a Professional Editor. Later on, I went on to learn scriptwriting (both for movies and for YouTube channels), and to date, I’m using these skills. And last year, I started learning Data Analysis, and so far, it has been great. I might not be a master yet, but I’m definitely better at studying numbers and noticing the patterns that they create. Datasets now make so much more sense to me, and the more I work with them, the easier it is to get comfortable with them. Back when I started, it was so difficult for me. I was always confused when I saw dirty datasets, and I didn’t even know how to proceed. But not anymore. All that is handled now. I’m a professional. ![IMG_20230614_001552~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23tRvTBZpgMXD3YFgvFtSSyEaQtZDEsP63SVWhMJWpPFpvrAEYnTqJrHbgAdB1YHMGxvT.jpg) So, what am I learning now? I guess my answer is that I’m neither learning nor unlearning, I’m currently relearning. Growing up, one of the things I lost to my childhood and teenage years was my love for reading. Not just novels, but motivational and religious books as well. I still read, but it’s mostly once in a while, and even then, it has to be by a really famous person. Back in the day, I used to give every book a chance. I believed that if you thought it was good enough to publish, I had to assume it would be good enough to read. But going to school changed all that for me, and since then, it’s been hard finding time to read. However, this year, I decided to take up that habit once again. Last year, I was using ebooks, chiefly because of their audio features, but that’s not as immersive as I’d like. I want to curl up on my couch with a physical book and read in the quiet of my home. I miss those days, and I want to bring them back. This used to be a way of life, adulthood took it from me. But I’m taking it back. I’m going back to reading regularly. And for now, my target is one book per month. Since the year started, I’ve only been able to finish one, but by making this post, I’m putting it out there and making it final. I’m going back to how it used to be! ![IMG_20231006_1557032.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23xKvQZMjA9MqEStLnmEFAz5HZ9T4q4mXjN5JeJC4B83YrszGQdmT3PikGJAmqyjQyfeG.jpg) ***
Thank you for reading. Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments below, I would love to know what you’re thinking. Till we meet in the next post.
***
Watch My Engaging Stories on: [Facebook](https://web.facebook.com/brunokemaofficial), [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@bruno_kema), and [TikTok]( https://www.tiktok.com/@bruno_kema?_r=1&_t=ZN-91fKKHrMpuw).
***
N.B: All images used in this post are mine. The thumbnail was designed using Canva.
***

body.title: The Lush Greenery Mountains of Mt. Turong-Turong
body.body:
![LEAD PHOTO BLOG (4).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/243WPu8ta6FSEJMsdqVPKu54cV6Yg8fW3rm2HG3KyYj8ZyhcUAiGP9igkkdMUKQLcycHQ.jpg)

The day started when the sun was still sleeping tight, on a Sunday dawn. The stars were twinkling on the dark skies and the wind was cold. We travelled to the neighboring municipality to join a climb-for-a-cause activity to help the community of San Antonio, Tukuran, Zamboanga del Sur.
First and foremost, all volunteers gathered at the municipality office to confirm our payment and presence. After the checking of attendance, we were now set to travel an hour through riding the municipality's vehicles.


![6154700603918061907.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/23tknMWN7quHjp2Q5uZASiHAX15WXZjNu1MLv22HNQifo5B7kLpTmNqikgSWNU5KELBZA.jpg)

It was still dark when we reached the Mt. Turong-Turong jumpoff, the community of San Antonio. The wind was so cold and the droplets from the fogs were kissing our skin.  The organizers of the activity created a short preliminary program, and it started with a prayer, a zumba, and another attendance checking. A trekking stick made by the locals, fruits, and water were part of the itineraries, so it was distributed by the organizers to the volunteers. The community rules were also read by the Barangay Captain and the volunteers were grouped by ten with a tour-guide for each group.


![6154700603918061727.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/244KRFme1HWcPaTf2TAWjtwWPFWP7Uc7xzovkZMpi2yeMDPojwpLvLsyY7cUHeP27PAC5.jpg)
An hour and a half before the sunrise when the hike started. The trail was so steep that the first five minutes of the hike felt like our lungs were running out of oxygen. The other volunteers were using flashlights but I was just using the light of the moon to see the trail. Some volunteers almost surrendered and some did really surrender, and they just wait at the bottom because they could not climb the ascent.

![6154570260250562001.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/242Y5cmQJAmy69Spy1FDg1whXs39uUJy1RjMHGCz4bgLQ9FeyVvdjgTu1UpPs2asSoBA3.jpg)

In order to reach the peak, we needed to climb two mountains. When our group reached the second mountain, the wind started to blew stronger and stronger. I was knocked down by the wind for a multiple times and I almost fell from the mountain, luckily, I got hold unto the grasses. I did not think of being wounded because these tall grasses were slightly sharp, all I thought was only not to fell because it was really dark, they could not find me if I fall because I had no flashlight.


![6154570260250562002.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/23ywiQApMXvqkePmLPLB84thEcQZZC2pVb1BbZM6VPsWmRsHVRbg8x3fmG7b47ig9qx16.jpg)
The sunrise was so beautiful that it fully captured my heart and my soul. Everyone was taking pictures and admiring the view from the peak of Mt. Turong-Turong. Every step and hard-breathing was worth it. Nothing compares to the feeling of being at the mountain top.


![6154570260250561996.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/23y8qrVywFqyVSUt2Ppg6VGqHLkH4PeftSDrNLxSomyoXhqc61kfMZHccobcYEDLAQgV9.jpg)
I am grateful to have this trekking stick made by the locals of San Antonio, if it wasn't for it, the wind my blow me away, and I may wouldn't reach the peak. I will forever treasure this meaningful souvenir. And by the way, they also gave us an appreciation certificate because they said our registration money were big help as donations, but little did they know, we appreciate them more for taking care of this paradise. I'm gonna say it here, \

![6154570260250561972.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/EqL6uEiS2wUZrHMmXj1YyCDyDFwKrbD2Wpb1jzsQSCa3E7aYJVYhqQS5ofnp2hvcJnK.jpg)
We took a picture again when the sun was up because our first picture was taken when it was still dark. This picture was taken on six in the morning and the wind was still blowing strong while the sun was kissing our cheeks. 
It was really an awesome experience at the lush greenery mountains of Mt. Turong-Turong. I hope you could experience the peak of this mountain too!



![6154570260250561981.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/243zdWR7UvJZC3Zd1LkfpGdDhDVeWzUKkLvfiZLgt1ibaWBo4jnFFzTBq953qQA5K9BEz.jpg)

![6154251084050927101.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/EqDk4XynkpyYfTuGpCrMYab6qGztF6ufdF7F1rinR8Z6ct7YibYN1TmX7AVAGtxJXDz.jpg)


![6154570260250561971.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arenaofroses/EpxrF6CtuMhn3qnu6DbyxetLHCAiALrQAc6GQakfGNKUHEf3htoegSrrfj49wQFTRv4.jpg)

I hope you enjoy our blog today. See you next time<3
P.S. Lead photo was edited using Canva.

body.title: This is what Valencia was like before and this is what it is like now [ESP/ENG]
body.body:
![Cream Red Vintage Retro Music Presentation (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23x1MzwkQa1zqQNAFpsdpK4xregCk6GWdiXYpdbTfxFXZCSW5BoqGfmVCZ3FJgsL65Djn.jpg)
(Cover designed by me in canva editor)
>Portada diseñada por mi en el editor de Canva

I've always loved history, trivia, and all that. In fact, I'm so curious that I'm always researching things, and that's how my YouTube channel, \

was born. However, lately, I've been incredibly curious to discover things about the past of my own surroundings, the city where I live, Valencia (in Venezuela). When I walked through the historic center, I couldn't stop wondering what it looked like many years ago, and wow! What a surprise I got when I started researching historical facts, even finding photographic material that helped me get a better understanding. So, I set out to visit each of the places that seemed most emblematic and with an interesting history. That day, I toured with my mom while I told her all these details, and now I'd like to share them with you. So, hop in the time machine and join me on this historical tourism adventure!\n\n>Siempre he amado la historia, las curiosidades y todo eso, de hecho, es tal mi curiosidad que siempre estoy investigando cosas, y de allí nació mi canal de youtube \

sin embargo últimamente se ha desatado una enorme curiosidad en mi por descubrir cosas del pasado de mi propio entorno, la ciudad en la que vivo, Valencia (de Venezuela) cuando caminaba por el centro histórico no dejaba de preguntarme como se vería muchos años atrás, y ¡Wow! Vaya sorpresa la que me llevé cuando empecé a investigar datos históricos, encontrando incluso material fotográfico que me ayudaron a tener un mejor contexto, así que me di a la tarea de visitar cada uno de los lugares que me parecieron más emblemáticos y con una historia interesante. Ese día hice el recorrido junto con mi mamá mientras yo le iba contando todos estos datos, y ahora me gustaría compartirlos con ustedes, así que súbanse a la máquina del tiempo y acompáñenme en esta aventura de turismo histórico.

![bv.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/48Z7ryN5FxLMaGrQmRwAJ2GeRpTNLD7V2jZffXxJLwD3NYpq9evp2HsG9AK7cvuC4m.png)

That wall you see in the background with a beautiful mural depicting part of Venezuela's history is now a police station located in the heart of Valencia's historic center, across from Plaza Bolívar. But you won't believe what was there before...

>Esa pared que ustedes ven al fondo con un mural precioso que muestra parte de la historia de Venezuela, es actualmente una estación de policía que está en pleno casco histórico de Valencia, frente a la plaza Bolívar, pero ustedes no creerán lo que había allí antes...
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.35 AM (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EpEJoK7ZoMEQxL2GKzXVZXrpmAEjdBaiqm8pugr2Z823TaPw1SwUMGqHmZR8BUc7zwe.jpeg)

This was the Town Hall, a stately two-story mansion with multiple balconies, dating back to colonial times. It served as the city hall during both the colonial and republican eras. As I understand it, in the 1920s, during the oil boom when the country was captivated by the promise of progress, they wanted to give the building a facelift. So, under the administration of then-President (dictator) Juan Vicente Gómez, the building was demolished—some say completely, others only partially. The Municipal Palace was then built on the site, which was also demolished in the 1970s to give the city a more \

feel. However, since they could never agree on what to build there next, it became a parking lot and is now a police station.

\n\n>Se trataba de La Casa Consistorial, la cuál databa de los tiempos de la colonia, una casona señorial de dos pisos y múltiples balcones, era allí donde funcionaba el ayuntamiento de la ciudad en los tiempos de la colonia y de la republica. Según tengo entendido, en los años 20, cuando empezó todo ese auge del petróleo y el país estaba fascinado bajo el hechizo del progreso, querían darle una nueva cara al edificio, así que bajo el mandato del entonces presidente (dictador) Juan Vicente Gómez, el edificio fue demolido, algunos dicen que total y otros dicen que parcialmente, luego se construyó allí el Palacio Municipal, el cual fue demolido también en los años 70, en aras de darle un aire más \

a la ciudad, pero como nunca se pusieron de acuerdo en lo que construirían allí posteriormente, se convirtió en un estacionamiento y actualmente en una estación de policía.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23zS9heDQhrYuQARemAX24sQRtjGZhex4AVuyX8nn9R1XKCwpcxKEF2Xh6uTN3vT8ankF.png)
[Casa Consistorial](https://tmp133418770wordpresscom.wordpress.com/2019/10/27/el-palacio-municipal-y-enrique-bernardo-nunez/)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23z7SpF7rq3Ai1EhneMVSp7kgiCN48WYLse6qX2hrLNLJcD1F63Uhxs3UaeoEWnJpNsjM.png)
[Palacio Municipal construido en 1928](https://juanvicentegomezpresidente.blogspot.com/2021/07/palacio-municipal-de-valencia-venezuela.html)

Walking north through Plaza Bolívar before reaching Avenida Cedeño, the city still preserves a vestige of that building constructed in 1928. The architect in charge of the City Hall project built his house as a kind of \

of the building; it's not exactly the same, but it's quite similar. Currently, it functions as a women's clothing and lingerie store. It's a little sad to see that it wasn't designated as a museum, but at least it's gratifying to see that they respected its facade and that it retains many elements from that era, including the sign that reads \

\n\n>Subiendo por la plaza Bolívar en sentido norte antes de llegar a la avenida Cedeño, la ciudad aún conserva un vestigio de ese edificio construido en 1928, ya que el arquitecto encargado del proyecto de construcción del Palacio Municipal, construyó su casa como una especie de \

del edificio de ayuntamiento, no es exactamente igual pero se le parece bastante, actualmente funciona como una tienda de ropa y lencería femenina, da un poco de tristeza ver que no se destinó como un museo, pero al menos complace ver que respetaron su fachada y que conserva muchos elementos de esa época, incluso el letrero que reza \

![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.21 AM (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EonmXhRZpN4sQ5KvWEmW3hxNxCgX1ZTSGrv6NbVe3MVokqB7ur9vgBKcFVUNFS5ufuP.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.22 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EoeFvtLdQov6nh2YNyNu4E6FfxRYdKwT5ANXQ6c3egzphLAxKfPwJNnFgittLNDSE2Y.jpeg)

Right in the middle of Plaza Bolívar, on one of the corners, we have the Victoria Tower, a small and colorful building that currently goes completely unnoticed, it doesn't attract attention at all, some of its letters are even falling off, but at one time it was the most modern and tallest in the city, however, would you believe me if I told you that there, before the construction of that building, there was once a majestic five-star hotel called the Hotel Alemán?

>En plena plaza Bolívar, en una de las esquinas tenemos la Torre Victoria, un edificio pequeño y colorido que actualmente pasa completamente desapercibido, ni llama la atención en lo absoluto, incluso algunas de sus letras se están cayendo, pero en su momento llegó a ser el más moderno y alto de la ciudad, sin embargo ¿ustedes me creerían si yo les dijera que allí, antes de la construcción de ese edificio estuvo alguna vez un majestuoso hotel cinco estrellas que se llamaba Hotel Alemán?
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.38.22 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23yd459pvg4jAdZaU4ESUCmLtQQzWihj2hhQw3ZqA9qRGkhiTX7VvaG6hnoySTQA3mpQt.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.38.25 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EowH4k5UETJdiDqE6hkYyHC5ayjczGtavLNqnT4piSzsMeuPGdFj8sMoChSUsLiXDnu.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.38.07 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EoyPzjFfjVHK2XyWad49rrmmeQav9o6yPnCRQ3L5ShyiEQX7E4ryXyA7bTVKiyt7R7W.jpeg)

According to the Facebook page \

(I recommend visiting it if you love history as much as I do), the majestic Hotel San Rafael once stood there, later renamed Hotel Alemán and finally Hotel Victoria (which gave the current building its name). The hotel was very exclusive and hosted many renowned figures of its time; it's even said to have housed two spies from World War II (though this is speculation, nothing concrete, but still interesting 😁). But, again, the people of Valencia at that time (1969) were obsessed with giving the city a more modern look 🙄 so they ended up demolishing the building to construct the tower we have now. How disappointing, right? It's supposed to be the historic center; it doesn't have to look modern.

\n\n>Según la página de facebook \

(recomiendo visitarla si les gusta la historia tanto como a mi) dice que allí funcionó el majestuoso Hotel San Rafael, que posteriormente pasó a llamarse: Hotel Alemán y finalmente Hotel Victoria (lo que le dio nombre al actual edificio) el hotel era muy exclusivo y llegó a recibir a personas de mucho renombre en su época, incluso se cuenta que llegó a alojar a dos espías de la segunda guerra mundial (aunque esto es una especulación, no ha nada en concreto pero igual es interesante 😁) pero, de nuevo, los Valencianos de aquellos tiempos (1969) estaban obsesionados con darle una cara más moderna a la ciudad 🙄 así terminaron demoliendo el edificio para construir la torre que tenemos actualmente. Qué decepcionante, ¿No? Se supone que es el casco histórico, no tiene porqué verse moderno.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23yTj8Nb3qQEG9gcLN6vVtnV8T4u8vRiYujUE12NvNRVG5R7G9uRV3NBKucuBjES1UpLv.png)
[Antiguo Hotel Victoria](https://www.facebook.com/groups/121930817952147/posts/4177829175695604/)

And finally, (for now) I bring you the most shocking story. This building you see behind me is currently a modern clothing store called Mundo Total (although it retains its original facade). You can even see me inside the store, surrounded by various items. I myself have shopped at that store several times, and even at that moment I was with my mom choosing gifts for my dad's birthday. But many of those customers who were there with us, as well as the workers and even the owners, are possibly unaware of the grim history hidden there, what happened in colonial times in that same place when it was the home of the Malpica family.

>Y finalmente, (Por ahora) les traigo la historia más impactante, este edificio que ven a mis espaldas es actualmente una moderna tienda de ropa llamada Mundo Total (aunque conserva su fachada original), incluso pueden verme en el interior de la tienda, rodeada de artículos varios, yo misma he comprado en esa tienda varias veces, e incluso en ese momento estaba con mi mamá eligiendo regalos para el cumpleaños de mi papá, pero muchos de esos clientes que estaban allí con nosotras, así como los trabajadores e incluso los dueños, posiblemente ignoran la tétrica historia que se esconde allí, lo que sucedió en los tiempos de la colonia en ese mismo lugar cuando era el hogar de la familia Malpica.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.30 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/EonkwpJ5owg3P1hKRnb6KC6vwdZDY1eiUxjf8GLaPkAn95EcziVspMtQ6i9NWzAwSBJ.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.31 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23z7WfvezePCPaoQxEWK2ofzsCworMjffUTbjLkGZwRN7PVHxauq9pLCrVvB6Wf8RLEpL.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.37.26 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/241tdZQrLaWZaEAXKWrFPU2TMnTiuioHcmD3ARzunYCSw9RBNEhWQGgajDKfPjYqFUxWK.jpeg)

In 1814, Venezuela was in the midst of its war of independence. José Tomás Boves, a leader of the royalist army, hated Simón Bolívar for being a \

a member of the Venezuelan aristocracy at the time. Boves wanted to reconquer Valencia (which Bolívar had already liberated). To do this, he besieged the city, surrounding it on all sides and cutting off its resources. Sooner or later, the population surrendered, and it is said that Boves swore to respect the rights of all citizens. But to celebrate his victory, he wanted to throw a ball, and he did so at the home of one of the richest men in the city, nicknamed \

Malpica (the current store). The Valencian bourgeoisie were forcibly invited to this event, and at a certain point, Boves ordered his musicians to play a Joropo (traditional Venezuelan music) called \

To its rhythm, he forced the ladies to dance with members of his army (Boves's army) while he murdered the gentlemen. Afterward, the ladies were raped and killed. However, there are many versions of this event. Some say that only a few gentlemen on a list were killed, and others say that the massacre took place at another house, not that one.

\n\n>En 1814 Venezuela se encontraba en plena guerra de independencia, José Tomas Boves que era un caudillo del ejército realista odiaba a Simón Bolívar por ser originalmente un mantuano, parte de la aristocracia venezolana de entonces, así que quiso reconquistar a Valencia (a la que Bolivar ya había liberado) para ello sitió la ciudad, cercándola por todas partes, dejándola sin recursos, así que tarde o temprano la población terminó rindiéndose y se dice que Boves juró respetar los derechos de todos los ciudadanos. Pero para celebrar la victoria quiso ofrecer un baile, y lo hizo en la casa de uno de los hombres más ricos de la ciudad a quién apodaban: “El Suizo” Malpica (la actual tienda) a ese evento fue invitada forzosamente la burguesía valenciana, y en determinado momento Boves ordenó a sus músicos tocar un Joropo (música típica venezolana) llamado \

y a su ritmo obligó a las damas a bailar con los miembros de su ejército (de Boves) mientras asesinaba a los caballeros, posteriormente ultrajaron a las damas y les dieron muerte. Sin embargo hay muchas versiones respecto a este hecho, algunos dicen que solo unos cuantos caballeros que estaban en una lista fueron asesinados, y otros dicen que el lugar de la masacre no fue esa casa sino otra.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23zbRaaMrmCpUY1w6kqipkkk2cb7uMKfKXpBvAeeavdNdEBDDgyQP2JVRF4VCqPc69AEE.png)
[Fuente](https://correodelara.com/julio-de-1814-boves-en-valencia-la-tragedia/)

And well friends, this was my historical tour through the streets and emblematic sites of my city, Valencia in Venezuela. Tell me if you would like to know more places like these, with a lot of history. I still have a long way to go to share with you if you wish.

body.title: 438 Days: Book Review
body.body:
#### Imagine being stuck at sea for over a year...

Its hard to imagine how one would survive such an ordeal. 

438 Days, by author Jonathan Franklin,  is about the true life story of how one man did just that.

![20260222_191300.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leaky20/23tvcM9N83zm5EQCNvUP83kQ8SPthkTPyQ8zyMSPDYnhv391Y7EVjC9P4gGr9LHTp3VZ5.jpg)

### <center>Brief Synopsis</center>

<hr>

*Note: This description contains only minor spoilers, like those that you would read from the description on the back of the book. That being said if you wanted to go in completely blind to this book with no information about it whatsoever, then I would avoid this part. Personally, I think your safe.* 

While fishing off the coast of Mexico in the open pacific, Salvador Alvarenga and his partner get caught in a major storm which sends them drifting endlessly into the open ocean. With not much food and water and very little supplies, the two men are forced to overcome countless obstacles that we normally take for granted, like how to get food and water, and basic shelter. 

This book was a very interesting read and another one of those true testaments about human survival in extreme conditions.  

![20260222_084812~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/leaky20/23uQnVqsJtGvbwHHmTtQwvZqsVnPDArmii1mo88Dzi4cCSWA427vB71Tpu8ZLPDQa8buW.jpg)

I read this book very quickly (for me), over the course of about three days. The weather was cold and frosty and I was warm on the couch curled up with the book. There is nothing better than reading a book by the fire on a cold day. 

Anyway, what I found most inspiring was Alvarengas attitude during the whole ordeal. He remained very positive throughout his time on the ocean, even despite the severe conditions. The challenges (both physical and mental) that he went through were mind boggling. I found that part to be very inspirational. 

This book was similar to a book i read last year called Adrift by Steven Callahan. He survived 76 days at sea and experienced a lot of the same thing in this book, though he had more supplies and gear. Both books were similar and very good but I think I preferred 438 Days slightly more. Overall I really enjoyed this book and would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes the true survival story genre. 

#### Let me know your thoughts in the comments. Have you read any good survival stories? Do you have any recommendations for me related to the survival genre. Let me know. Until next time, thanks for stopping by.

body.title: My Aunt and Uncle’s 21st Anniversary
body.body:
![4941.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iamboring/23zGm3GdsPL4ag7feAHc7nY3wojwddVLF4xPzXCdvwLUYQu747ypPSAqcmfYeWrUPPT5v.png)
This event happened last Friday, so sorry if I published it late. Anyway, I’d like to share what happened during my aunt and uncle’s wedding anniversary. It was a simple yet meaningful celebration as we commemorated it with my family from my mother’s side. They didn’t invite many visitors, and I’m glad we kept this tradition alive even though my grandparents have already passed away. Even though it wasn’t a huge party, we still made it a bit special.

# Preparation

![4942.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iamboring/23vsSMX7HWSsJBAo2FQwmZhpibQjYD9ybuNaobBQADadExRdjDZU4jhjTanaiak2tnvp1.png)

For the preparation, my mom made suman, puto, and kutsinta. Since my aunt wanted to reduce her workload, she outsourced it to my mom, which was a nice side hustle. After she arrived home, my mom was stressed when she lost the gas lock of her tricycle. When she visited the motor shop to ask about it, they told her that a mechanic still needed to attach the lock.

Anyway, I helped her wash the dishes and assist with cooking. I also helped call my younger brother and dad to ask how to deal with the gas lock. You know, driving isn’t my talent, especially after hearing about my classmate who died in a motorcycle accident. Of course, going to a mechanic would take time, so our only option for now was to use pliers.

# Foods Prepared

![4917.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iamboring/23tvZzfUA46dvWGCnGNcaHjFVFnSjtEtBgPYUdzztomwPo5YRhDKmtvSswn3Eoy2KVXkY.jpg)

Once everything was ready, we went to my late grandmother’s house. The foods prepared were pinakbet, suman, puto, adobo, rice, spaghetti, and soft drinks. As you can see, there were plenty of dishes, and taking pictures is a tradition that can’t be removed from our family.

By the way, I only ate puto, adobo, rice, and spaghetti. Among all the dishes, the adobo was the most outstanding and was consumed quickly since it was only five kilos. My mom said it wouldn’t have been consumed so fast if they had added at least three more kilos. I loved the spaghetti, although it was a bit cold. They prepared it at 4 PM but we only ate it at 7 PM while waiting for more guests. Even though it was already cold, it still tasted really good.

# Pictures

![4943.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iamboring/23tvZrTtgSZ8PjP9F11WuLas7PsodKBtPMmvqZppyFHjRkas7mQbHRKDapFQKTjnQHTXq.png)

There were unlimited pictures, of course. My aunt loves collecting photos and videos and later creating a CapCut video edit. She captured moments while we were eating, arriving, and before going home.

After I finished eating, I busied myself editing my YouTube video and playing some songs. I also played crossword puzzles to ease my boredom. Even while doing my own thing, it was still nice to be part of the celebration and see everyone enjoy the day.

The world is a world of offenses. Jesus Christ told us that in the world there will be offenses. He said that it will be impossible for us to think that there will not be offenses in the world. So, this is an instruction that there will always be occasions for someone to be offended as long as we are in the world. The world cannot be a perfect place because the evil one is still working. The Bible says that the devil goes about like a roaring lion seeking for whom he may devour. So, this devil turns this world into an offensive place. We must bear in our minds that there is no way we are going to escape the issue of offenses in the world.

What did our Lord Jesus Christ told us? He told us to always forgive those who offends us. Yes, offenses are inevitable but we must not allow the offenses to make us overcome of evil. We must overcome evil with good. We must not allow the bitterness of offenses to overcome us. We must overcome every offensive situation by love. Only love is the antidote for the various offenses that are in the world.

The reason why many people find it difficult to forgive others is because they are not working in love. We have the love of God in us because we are born of God. Let us express this love everywhere. Let us not cause offenses to others. Also let us not be weary to forgive those who sin against us. When we forgive, let us try to forget the bad things that people do to us. The Holy Spirit shall give us the ability to forgive all men always.

body.title: Work stays at work
body.body: On the way home from work, even the breeze tastes sweet. It’s such a blessing to have a job where work stays at work and life stays at life.\n\nWith an 8-hour workday and a 2-hour lunch break, I get four precious hours of \

after I clock out. I have so many hobbies—anything DIY catches my eye. Beading, clay modeling, painting... these are the little joys that fill my spare time. Sometimes I’ll pick up a book, but more often than not, I’m just scrolling through Douyin, Xiaohongshu, or Bilibili. Once I start watching videos, those four hours vanish in the blink of an eye. I am the master of my own time; I can choose instant gratification or delayed happiness. But occasionally, after a scrolling session, a wave of melancholy hits. As I’m falling asleep, I find myself questioning the ultimate meaning of life. At work, I can't check my phone. When things get slow, watching the clock tick by is actually quite painful. I’m the type of person who dreads having nothing to do. Time flies when I’m busy, but when I’m idle, every second feels like an eternity.

Hi Actifit Friends.
I hope you all are well, I am also well. Today, it was very hot here again in our city, but we had planned to visit our favorite place again so that we could go here and change our minds a little and relax a little, because in life, every person has many problems and they continue with time and in the same way, we have to take them with us and in some places, we have to take care of many things.
![IMG_20260309_150945.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPFQ5LTTBMHWCJnfff9hbo4PQZVMvFe3u8DsLvXhDp3E9/IMG_20260309_150945.jpg)
Traveling on a motorcycle in summer is not easy at all, especially when we have to go to such rural areas because the summers are hotter in the villages and the winters are colder. So what I want to say here is that the coming time is going to be much hotter in our country because earlier our city was colder and there was less heat, but now the time has changed, so there are more summers and less winters.
So what I want to say here is that if we look at the temperature at this time, it is getting quite high and the environment of the whole world is also changing. Our city is more famous for its heat. First of all, as per our habit, we had also taken permission from them. We had not seen this place before and after a long time, it looked much more beautiful and we were enjoying it a lot because it is a fact that the coming time is going to be very busy.

body.title: Mensaje diario de 5 minutos-¿que comió?/ Daily 5 minute message-  he ate what?
body.body:
> Esta mañana un comportamiento extraño hizo una de las mascotas. Un perrito que vive para comer no salio corriendo como cada mañana para buscar su plato. Eso me hizo pensar rápidamente en que comió ayer. Que le cayo tan mal, que no quiere comer su perrarina. Eso fue extraño en verdad, las ganas de comer son una medida del estado de salud de las mascotas. Ellas siempre tienen hambre, siempre quieren comer. Así que me puse a pensar en si había comido algo diferente, si se me había caído algo al piso. Lo único que comió extra según mi hijo fue un trozo de pan que el se estaba comiendo y se le cayo y las mascota fue más rápida que él, agarrándolo. Yo creo que no tuvo ganas de quitárselo, de verdad pensó que no le caería mal. Estoy segura que dentro de un rato comerá tranquilamente. Otras veces a presentado estas fallas en sus ganas de comer, que rápido se le pasan comiendo monte de mi jardín. El pan es una de las harinas que le cae muy mal a los perros, pero ellos simplemente les encanta y nosotros le damos de nuestra propia comida creyendo que lo estamos haciendo bien. Luego vienen las complicaciones, porque las mascotas siempre tienen ganas de comer. Ya se le esta pasando fue a buscar su plato, lo cual es una señal de que ya tienen apetito.
***
Este texto corresponde a mi participación en el reto diario del amigo @latino.romano y @mariannewest [post](https://hive.blog/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/10-march-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3038-he-ate-what) **ENGLISH VERSION**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZwq8J5Jhh4GxVXMu8VGsBP8o3jLp7d18XedDkr8UQXUw/imagen.png)
This morning one of the pets acted strangely. A little dog who lives to eat didn't run out to find his food bowl as usual. That immediately made me wonder what he ate yesterday. What made him so sick that he didn't want to eat his dog food? It was really strange; a pet's appetite is a good indicator of their health. They're always hungry, always want to eat. So I started wondering if he'd eaten something different, if I'd dropped something on the floor. The only thing he ate extra, according to my son, was a piece of bread he was eating that fell, and the pet was faster than him, grabbing it. I think he didn't feel like taking it back; I really thought it wouldn't upset his stomach. I'm sure he'll eat normally in a little while. Other times he's had these bouts of losing his appetite, but they quickly disappear when he eats weeds from my garden. Bread is one of the flours that dogs don't tolerate well, but they simply love it, and we give them our own food thinking we're doing the right thing. Then come the complications, because pets are always hungry. He's already gone to get his food bowl, which is a sign that he's hungry again.
***
This text corresponds to my participation in the daily challenge of my friend @improv, @felt.buzz, @latino.romano and @mariannewest [post](https://hive.blog/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/10-march-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3038-he-ate-what)

body.body:
Hi everyone,

When I visited this disused underground quarry with my guys @flav_explore & Captain Shlag in January 2024, I saw that spot and I promised myself not to leave this place without taking a couple of shots here.

The entire location was bigger than expected and we took a lot of time to explore it.

For that specific picture, I tried to manage with the natural light coming from the extraction well and a very open shutter. I used my iridescent magic wand and a tiny white LED to draw the abstract light-calligraphy :

![_MG_8519.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dawnoner/23vsBsN8NvESqgtNzeQ7SM54SPPfcFQCDYRxscFFZQfGXw6szLKSXGpK3xcDheaFcc76F.jpg)
<center>88s 16mm f/5 100 ISO</center>

![_MG_8529.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dawnoner/23tm7BpTGTsRqXXffFuBqULkrMteXMMnBv1Eui8PPKJNUDySc8h3erk7S1gWEdj2VKudF.jpg)
<center>232s 16mm f/4 100 ISO</center>

Lightpainting created in real time, captured to the camera in one single photographic frame. SOOC
No layers /no Photoshop / no editing except minor adjustments (lens correction profite, WB, contrast (+12)) and addition of my logo.

Gear :
Canon EOS 6D body
Canon EF 16-35mm f/4L IS II USM lens
Canon RC-E6 IR remote 
Zomei carbon tripod

January 2024

![Small Orange Divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lightpaintershub/EqQRymroVQGs2UcR1yGuXSx28smWccGYDQBnhkV4Savw1DL738xeitn5bbmiRMydoWx.png)

<center>**WHAT IS LIGHTPAINTING?**</center>
Lightpainting is a photographic technique in which exposures are made by moving a hand-held light source while taking a long exposure photograph, either to illuminate a subject or to shine a point of light directly at the camera, or by moving the camera itself during exposure. Nothing is added or removed in post processing.

<center>**Single exposure Light Art Photography
/nolayer /notricks /nophotoshop /no artificial intelligence**</center>

![Divider 5.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lightpaintershub/23xVEcaSEcACVXNajKEE1o7WZT8waYwyX6Frn2zscPzosaSbEdJNBkXsmkramYTrnHH9q.png)

body.title: Bluegrass State of Mind
body.body:
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/2458Dke5hRbjvTZktDimG71B8ww9P6pAAf1upGBWoctY1zMrQ3TVEScW2qvZpnuXsPPse.png)</center>

--------------------------

I can still remember one of the first times I ever visited Kentucky.  We were heading down to Oklahoma to visit one of my dad's old buddies from the Navy and we stopped for a day or two in the town where Mammoth Caves are.  A long long time ago there used to be an old west themed park called Guntown or Rifletown or something like that where you had to ride a chair lift to get up to it.  

From the moment I heard the story about how Mammoth Cave was discovered and I took the walk down the stairs in to the historic entrance, I knew there was something magical about Kentucky.  I've been back a few times since then.  My sister and her husband lived outside of Lexington for a while.  I still remember the thrill of driving 55 down the windy curvy back roads.  It's honestly some of the most beautiful country you have ever seen.  Horse farms with fences running for miles, black tobacco barns, bourbon.  You get the idea.

<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23zGW4bmsLssGRfU4vSoPzSQx1yXuKguGq2hjs2E4Y1mUZXY2N7RLCidusdR7THNcrf4z.png)</center>

---------------------------

I've driven through Kentucky a few times on my way down to Nashville, Tennessee as well, and there is always something that makes you want to stop and linger just a little longer in the Bluegrass State, no matter how eager you are to get down to Tennessee.  There is a reason the hills and hollers of Kentucky are so well know across the world, they are just amazing places.  It's like you are stepping into a whole different world.  

Don't get me wrong, I still love Michigan, and I wouldn't trade living here for pretty much anything, but there is just something really special about Kentucky and though I have only visited about half of the US, Kentucky would definitely be high up in the list if I was ever considering moving.

<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/242rkraxJeKtVEGjwx6PvDUUNKW25rK4HGX4VCVT8dZF53Vdj9UYqibAphKyj9P4ZJmEE.png)</center>

--------------------------

In case you haven't guessed, our musical road trip through the United States in alphabetical order takes us to Kentucky this week.  This is part of the #threetunetuesday prompt started by @ablaze.  It's been a lot of fun working through these posts and unlike some of the other states, Kentucky was almost too easy this week.  

<center><iframe width=\

allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

-----------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Czuc4q4axqU&list=RDCzuc4q4axqU&start_radio=1)

-----------------------

Call me crazy, but I have never been much of an Elvis fan.  Even when I was back in high school and there was this girl that was totally in love with him, I just couldn't bring myself to enjoy his music.  Sure, there were a couple of songs that I don't mind, but for the most part I just didn't see the appeal.  I used to hate the song \
, but thanks to South Park, I don't mind it too much anymore.  \

on the other hand is one that I have always enjoyed despite my disdain for the The King.

It's just a really good song and it has a good vibe to it.  What I mean is, it's kind of upbeat for a sad song, but it just works really well.  If you remember the rules of my posts, the song has to have the name of the state in the title or lyrics.  This one fits the bill on both counts.  If you have never heard Elvis or you aren't sure you like him, this is a good song to start with.  It might just change your mind.

<center><iframe width=\

allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

----------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dbU8pHS7W8w&list=RDdbU8pHS7W8w&start_radio=1)

----------------------------

I am unapologetically a huge Neil Diamond fan.  I just think he is pretty amazing as a singer and a songwriter. It's easy for people to get caught up in the whole \

schtick and forget that he has a whole catalog of songs that are just as good if not better than that one.  They might not have the same sing along value, but there is no question they are amazing songs. \n\n\

is one of those that I kind of feel like falls through the cracks at times.  It's got some good lyrics, a nice message, and just a pretty amazing feel to it.  There is a lot to love about this song.  I almost makes you want to go out and find a nice Kentucky woman of your own.  My friend told me once that Kentucky women always have great legs because of all the hills they have to walk up and down.\n\n<center><iframe width=\

allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

--------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sF0DV0MsYrQ&list=RDsF0DV0MsYrQ&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

Finally, that brings me to a song I know I have shared with you here before, but it just fits so well into this category that I would be crazy if I didn't include it here.  \

by Florida Georgia Line is just a fun rocking country song that you can't help but sing along to.  If you can work your way through some of the tongue twister lyrics that is.  I think one of my favorite parts of the chorus is how they slide that \

line in there.  You wouldn't think there were would be a way to fit it in and make it rhyme, but they totally do.

Just a quick reminder, all bourbon is whiskey, but not all whiskey is bourbon and Kentucky is basically the home of bourbon by law though many other distilleries in other states are co-opting the technique and the name.

As I said before, there are so many great places to visit in the United States, but there is just something extra special about Kentucky.  At least to me.  What do you think?

![1000032131.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EpGTbXxxcdit3SjUYV6WtA483fKGN1vUReFQyGbwDM7DTqXJkYjt6X5VwyeZdpHbf1i.png)

One thing I hate was facing people, but today I don't have a choice but to face a lot of people. There's a lot that I feel so awkward most of the times when facing them. I can't help it, I don't know why I become like this, too much shyness that I feel like just running away to hide. But I can't really do that because it is just me and Mommy F today here at home. My role for today is a \

in Mommy D's sari sari store (⁠^⁠.⁠_⁠.⁠^⁠)⁠ﾉ. 

I am accompanying Mommy F at the store because Mommy D had to visit her sister in Santa Teresa. Well, just the usual, they're surely having a bonding moments while i'm typing this. One of her sister is already 81 year old and Mommy F mentioned that she can't get up on the bed anymore ಥ⁠_⁠ಥ. And so, Mommy D and her other sister, Auntie Velyn take time to visit her on their home. It's been weeks since they last visit there so...

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EoGyM8SkrMxNztoxML1uiU3pEUf7SuJ3eGZo6Xx82oukjRWLsbSPHzKKe3r3bHf5wYT.jpg Mommy D stores sells a few things, mostly snacks, drinks and junk foods. We don't sell alcohol here because Mommy D feels like if she sell alcohol, some might chose to drink in front of the store. And what if a fight started? title.title: MONOMAD TUESDAY \
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcYTRR71v6962HJPh4NWEHbdMpFbwaiDoqowbwCBCgMmh/123457.jpg)

Hello Hive Community.

I hope you all are fine. I am also fine here. This is my entry for the #monomad challenge March 9th. Today I am making a post in the hive community after a break of four months. During these four months, there have also been huge ups and downs in the price of hive. But instead of discussing that topic, today's topic will be about black and white photography. Black and white photography is my favorite topic to make a post in the hive community. In today's post, you will see black and white photographs of Madurodam. Madurodam is a famous miniature park. In this park, the most important places of the Netherlands are shown in small size. Madurodam is a beautiful miniature park located in the city of The Hague in the South Holland province of the Netherlands.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPpq7W9wohwbHwXveZPmkTkPJ3ybiEe2BTdLXVdvRkS7Y/1_1.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU4Rt2GJ2Pgn2kZzn8jNPNhpoa4Kt3RsD6uZb8vQDGJPh/2_2.jpg)

The board with the name Madurodam can be seen in the two photographs above. As you enter the premises of Madurodam or from the parking lot, you can see this board. In this photograph you can see bicycles arranged in a row on a stand near the board. Madurodam is one of the most popular tourist attractions in the country. It is a great place to visit for tourists from abroad and locals alike. The park is known for its miniature models of cities, buildings, bridges, airports and many other places. These models are made very carefully so that they look almost like real places.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYYnrsHznp3wRTS8BEFnaa16prewHS9PXotmG4UCctRLs/3_3.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZBoiCbgzpjUSod8Rn3RubPxFbMe9iaxfjhPjR63L7GN9/4_4.jpg)

The first photograph of the two photographs above shows a tall signpost. This signpost has many white direction boards pointing to different cities around the world. Each board has the name of a city and the distance to that place written in numbers. Each arrow points in the direction of that city and shows the distance in kilometers. This type of signpost is often used in tourist areas to show how a place is connected to many other parts of the world. While the second photograph shows a small statue of a man standing among tall green plants near a wall covered in lush vegetation.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXXfcpWmJK1WDHmpZaWiEL5oQLJxkqR1Y4udw4fzYg6n2/5_5.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQsrsQumG9fgEo8tGWRHsjTukdBnLmbj6pEkuCprykvjN/6_6.jpg)

As can be seen in the two photographs above, the most special thing about Madurodam is that everything here is made in miniature form. Most of the buildings are made on a very small scale. Due to which these buildings are many times smaller than the real structures. Here small trains run on the tracks. And ships sail in small canals. And planes fly over the airport. These dynamic models make the park exciting and interesting. A huge number of people come here to visit this place, which can be seen in the photographs above.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNzw6px11qaE3mSDwBW7BgHv3feYxG35FARkY4dVUsz9Y/7_7.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmceTaHHcQbL2Wu9UE796gRdt3ZnEtMunbqdpcwt3F8LpE/8_8.jpg)

As captured in the photographs above, there is also a small train here. This train is the main attraction for children. The specialty of this small train is that this train does not need any track to run. It runs on the road, which the children enjoy to the fullest. This train is colorful, the main colors of which are red and yellow, which makes it attractive. Above I have presented two photographs, in which in the second photograph a child is expressing his joy by raising his thumb.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV75H5S1pVR1NAZB7AGY4mV3zBQzcgzPh6aTsdBFRRqNQ/9_9.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbM8mT231HcScxffAXMyowXs7qtPTU4QnhwfWGabZ178F/10_10.jpg)

This place is a perfect place to capture in photographs. I believe that Madurodam is not only a tourist attraction but also a place that helps people understand the Netherlands in a short time. By walking in this park, visitors can see many famous places of the country in a few hours. It is like displaying the famous places of the entire nation in a small model city. Another feature of this park is the gardens, small trees, flowers and green lawns here. These plants are carefully cut so that they remain small in size and match the small buildings. Which can be seen in the two photographs above.

I am very happy to make today's post because I have presented post on famous miniature park. I hope that my post will be accepted for the #monomad challenge March 9th.

I sincerely thank you for visiting and reading my post.

Hoy mi caminata por la ciudad fue realmente refrescante. El clima estaba perfecto, con una brisa suave que hacía que cada paso fuera aún más agradable. Mientras caminaba por el parque central, me encontré con un grupo de jóvenes que organizaban una clase de yoga al aire libre. Era inspirador ver a tantas personas reunidas, disfrutando del ejercicio y del aire libre. Al continuar mi recorrido, conocí a un anciano que solía ser fotógrafo. Me contó historias fascinantes sobre cómo capturaba momentos especiales en la ciudad en los años 70. Sus ojos brillaban al hablar de sus viejas cámaras y de las personas que había conocido a lo largo de los años. A lo largo del camino, también vi una exposición de arte callejero increíble. Artistas locales habían pintado murales vibrantes en las paredes, cada uno con un mensaje único sobre la comunidad. Fue un recordatorio de la creatividad que florece en la ciudad. Cada caminata me deja con la sensación de que hay tanto por descubrir y aprender de las personas que te rodean. Estoy deseando que llegue el próximo día para salir de nuevo y explorar. _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). title.title: A Common Monster with Crazy Damage!
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWspCnXK5Nit4mk2dMR9y9tXYLr3d2JkZy65J59SNW2Yk/magnificent_mollusk_thumbnail.png)



Hello **Splinterlands** warriors!

A new season always brings new colors to the arena. Sometimes it’s not only about rankings or season rewards, but also about the new cards that start appearing on the battlefield. And lately, one that has caught my attention comes from the escalation series—a sea creature with a rather majestic name: **Magnificent Mollusk**.

Honestly, the first time I saw the name, I smiled. “Magnificent Mollusk?” It sounds like an elegant sea snail. But after seeing its stats and abilities in the arena, I realized one thing immediately: this snail is not just a decorative sea creature… it’s a walking cannon.





Magnificent Mollusk is a monster from the Death element that belongs to the escalation series with a **mana cost of 13**. For a **common** monster, that’s quite a large mana cost. Usually when a card reaches numbers like that, our expectations rise as well.



And Mollusk does not disappoint.

It comes with **a massive ranged attack**, reaching up to **6 damage**. That’s not a small number in Splinterlands. In many situations, a single shot is enough to take away half of an enemy monster’s health.

On top of that, it has **speed 4**, which I think is quite important. With that speed, it often gets the chance to attack first in each round.

In a strategy game like Splinterlands, striking first can sometimes be just as important as striking hard.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYd9NPgyiFQkKtfp7bEpwBpv7WRSq6crCK6sz2YXKvFRe/magnificent_mollusk_stats.png)</center>

What makes Magnificent Mollusk even more interesting is the abilities it gains as it levels up.

At **level 5**, it gains **Demoralize**. This ability reduces the melee attack power of all enemy monsters. So not only does it deal damage from afar, it also weakens the enemy team at the same time.

Then at **max level**, it unlocks a fairly unique ability: **Apex Strike**.

This ability makes Mollusk target the **enemy monster with the highest power**. In other words, it acts like a sniper that immediately locks onto the biggest threat on the enemy team.

Personally, I find this very interesting. Normally we rely on positioning or other abilities to reach certain targets. But with Apex Strike, Mollusk seems to already know exactly who needs to be taken down first.

---

## The Battle That Taught Me Something

I once experienced the power of this card firsthand in a battle.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWfummE5Seb3PBVicR7VpRA4k1XiVuv9nxL525gdMDGKa/round_1.png)


Interestingly, our strategies were actually quite similar.

We both anticipated the possibility that the opponent might use magic attack debuffs. So each team brought one ranged monster as the main damage source.

On my team, I used **Meriput Slinger** with **4 ranged attack**.

Meanwhile, my opponent… brought **Magnificent Mollusk** with **6 ranged attack**.

At the start of the round, the battle felt balanced. Our team compositions were quite similar, and the strategies were not too different.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdmju4xkUb8xVkYBGobopg14w2ZpUsMxcYyBv2Ky3tMWj/round_2.png)


But then, one by one, Mollusk’s attacks started to show their impact.

Six damage from a single shot felt like a sledgehammer. Every time it hit my team, it felt like we lost momentum. Monsters that should have survived two rounds suddenly fell much faster.

And that’s when I realized something: sometimes **a difference of just two damage points can completely change the direction of a match**.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaS35mFy6KibB4dw2Qf97UCwZh92ERYbUVh4hHgnCSuto/round_end.png)


In the end, even though the battle was intense, I had to let the victory go to my opponent.

You can see the battle here:
<center> 👉  [**LINK BATTLE**](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_00852f7230443a548c360ba647ff27d0?ref=rqr4)  👈</center>


Watching the replay afterward, I could only think to myself, “Alright… this snail is actually really dangerous.”

---

## Interesting Things About Magnificent Mollusk

After seeing and experiencing it in the arena, I noticed several key strengths of this card:

* **Very high ranged damage** for a common monster
* **Decent speed**, allowing it to attack first frequently
* **Demoralize** helps weaken melee-heavy enemy teams
* **Apex Strike** focuses on the most dangerous enemy target

This combination makes Mollusk not just a typical damage dealer, but also **a hunter of the enemy’s biggest threats**.

---

## Lessons From This Battle

Fighting against Magnificent Mollusk taught me a simple lesson:

In Splinterlands, we often focus on many things—ability combinations, monster positioning, or rulesets. But sometimes what determines victory is something very simple: **enough damage at the right moment**.

And Mollusk has exactly that.

In my opinion, Magnificent Mollusk works very well in:

* **Medium to high mana battles**
* Formations that need **strong ranged damage**
* Teams that want to quickly eliminate the **enemy’s strongest monster**

A strategy worth trying is placing it in the backline with a strong tank protecting the front, allowing it to keep firing without interruption.

In short, don’t be fooled by its status as a common monster.

Because in the Splinterlands arena, sometimes **the calm-looking sea creature is the one carrying the biggest cannon**.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuXxp6GBhwB1HpXvoabLn8Dt8QaRKSe1WNYDzqX1v6Vk/chaos_logo.png)



Talk about Splinterlands,
If you haven't tried out this fantastic game called Splinterlands yet, I invite you to [**Join**](https://splinterlands.com?ref=rqr4).
It's free, but you'll need to invest in a beginning deck or buy gaming cards to gain real assets like cards and tokens. 

___


If you already joined the splinterlands, and are looking for a place to grow. We need **YOU**. We are a chill, social guild looking for a few more active members! If you think you might be a fit, join us in our [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/5u638vHPVh)

title.title: soon it will be spring
title.body:
# soon it will be spring Good Morning Another wishful thinking post again, the long range forecast does show some warming up and a few rainy days So I remain hopeful as I post this that soon I will be getting out and about with my camera for photo walks, its been a long tough winter and my camera has been sitting in my camera bag for far too long. Well an update before I share this, we have had a couple of nice days without rain where i could have got out for a walk, but those days I had other things I had to do and couldnt find time to get out for a photo walk, so again I say hopefully soon, perhaps even today :) Whats your favorite season? I used to say I do not really have a favorite season, I loved them all and the variety they bring, but that has changed for me over the last few years. With age and health issues I feel the cold more these days and tend to get stuck indoors over winter, so thats easy to scratch out of contention. The other three seasons I still enjoy, some complain about the heat in summer, but that doesn't bother me so much, perhaps because I like going for early morning walks thats doesnt bother me, even the odd time I go out for ealks during the day, mind you that said I try to avoid being in the sun for long, have had too many bits of skin cancer removed, so I avoid direct sunlight for the most part, or when I do cover up withg sunscreen and often a light jacket Fall I do love with all the colors it brings, but also find it as Mother nature teasing us before the long cold grey winter months coming after, and last year Autumn/Fall seemed so short. Spo right now as I am looking forward to it I think I will have to say Spring is my favorite season When the flowers and blossoms appear such as in this first shot of a little green area in the historic district downtown

Hello everyone! 

Today, I want to share with you my new art work. It's a random portrait drawing of a beautiful young woman wearing weavon.


The portrait was done with a blue ballpoint pen on a cardboard paper. I used scribble technique to create this piece. 

###### Below are my step-by-step processes:
