title.title: Running, podcasts and a growing garden [EN/FR]
title.body:
Hello Hive!

It is Tuesday. And when it is Tuesday, it means Koh-Lanta on TV tonight. It is almost our only exception. We never watch TV. We never watch reality TV either… except this show.

To be honest, we often stop watching after a few weeks. But it creates a small ritual. And those little rituals, in the end, feel really good.

We prepare something good to eat, we settle down quietly… and tonight precisely, we are going to make shawarmas. We actually need to prepare the bread today.

@altheana or I might make a small recipe if someone is interested!

Yesterday, I worked on preparing a quote to create a Google Ads campaign for a tourism company. I was quite proud of the final document I sent. Right now, I enjoy working on SEO / SEA / GEO more than doing classic website editing.

I have phases. And right now, I am clearly in the one where I prefer maths, data and numbers to the creativity of web design. It probably comes from the fact that I have a bit of trouble concentrating these days.

We also did a running session yesterday. On my side, I ran 5.6 km. I was normally supposed to stop around 4.9 km. But just before passing again in front of the house, I turned into a small path to add a bit more distance.

During that running session, I listened to two podcasts.

The first one talked about SEO in the age of AI. And therefore GEO, Generative Engine Optimization. In a world where the web as we know it, with its ten blue links on Google, is disappearing… how can we get cited by AIs?

AIs cite your company or your site when they believe they can trust you. And that trust, they build it by observing if other entities talk about you.

And how do other entities talk about you?
When you participate in interviews.
When you publish on social networks.
When you build a brand.
When you share your ideas and your experience.

An AI starts to consider you credible when it sees that you have experience in your field, for example with data or concrete results on your site, and when it perceives that you are human, connected to other humans.

The second podcast was about the future of companies 100% driven by AI.

The question was simple: if AIs can do everything for you, analyze data faster, produce content, automate tasks, what is your added value then?

Will leaders, whose role was often to quickly analyze information and make cold decisions, be replaced?

The answer was rather nuanced. No… except for companies that refuse to take the AI turn. Those ones indeed risk being overtaken.

According to the author of the podcast, the key skills for the coming years would actually be quite human: knowing how to pilot technology with discernment and knowing how to lead teams with real empathy.

If AI becomes better and better at explaining *how* to do things, the role of the leader becomes mainly to explain *why* we do them.

Coming back from that run, we went to the vegetable garden to see if the peas and the spinach were starting to come out of the ground.

And good surprise: the spinach is starting to come out! For now they are very small shoots. I just hope I am not confusing them with grass growing…

![3f3ddb01-b08e-4e86-af81-20e4ef28fae2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/genesisledger/EoEq76VxSiFufG5bcSWy9ScthLXj6UaYPfUK6F3HWPhhUS68EybT3mmxkWkELtfGeKL.jpg)

We also harvested a bit of kale for lunch. If you can grow some at home, or simply buy some, go for it.

You wash the leaves, you put barely one tablespoon of olive oil in a pan with garlic and salt, then you let everything cook for 10 to 15 minutes.

It is simple. And it is delicious.

In the afternoon, I had a meeting and a few other things to move forward on for work.

Have a nice day Hive!


---

### Version Française

---

Bonjour Hive !

Nous sommes mardi. Et qui dit mardi, dit Koh-Lanta ce soir à la télé. C’est presque notre seule exception. Nous ne regardons jamais la télé. Nous ne regardons jamais de télé-réalité non plus… sauf cette émission.

Pour être honnête, on décroche souvent au bout de quelques semaines. Mais ça crée un petit rituel. Et ces petits rituels, finalement, font beaucoup de bien.

On prépare quelque chose de bon à manger, on s’installe tranquillement… et ce soir justement, on va se faire des shawarmas. Il faut d’ailleurs qu’on prépare le pain aujourd’hui.

@altheana ou moi ferons peut-être une petite recette si ça intéresse quelqu’un !

Hier, j’ai travaillé sur l’élaboration d’un devis pour créer une campagne Google Ads destinée à une compagnie touristique. J’étais plutôt fier du document final que j’ai envoyé. En ce moment, je prends plus de plaisir à travailler sur du SEO / SEA / GEO qu’à faire de l’édition de site classique.

J’ai un peu des phases. Et en ce moment, je suis clairement dans celle où je préfère les maths, les données et les chiffres à la créativité de la conception web. Ça vient sans doute du fait que j’ai un peu de mal à me concentrer ces derniers temps.

Nous avons aussi fait une séance de running hier. De mon côté, j’ai fait 5,6 km. Je devais normalement m’arrêter vers 4,9 km. Mais juste avant de repasser devant la maison, j’ai bifurqué dans un petit chemin pour rallonger un peu la sortie.

Pendant cette séance, j’ai écouté deux podcasts.

Le premier parlait du SEO à l’ère de l’IA. Et donc du GEO, Generative Engine Optimization. Dans un monde où le web tel qu’on le connaît, avec ses dix liens bleus sur Google, est en train de disparaître… comment faire pour être cité par les IA ?

Les IA citent votre entreprise ou votre site quand elles estiment pouvoir vous faire confiance. Et cette confiance, elles la construisent en observant si d’autres entités parlent de vous.

Et comment d’autres entités parlent de vous ?
Quand vous participez à des interviews.
Quand vous publiez sur les réseaux sociaux.
Quand vous développez une marque.
Quand vous partagez vos idées et votre expérience.

Une IA commence à vous considérer comme crédible quand elle voit que vous avez de l’expérience dans votre domaine, par exemple avec des données ou des résultats concrets sur votre site, et quand elle perçoit que vous êtes humain, connecté à d’autres humains.

Le second podcast portait sur l’avenir des entreprises 100 % pilotées par l’IA.

La question était simple : si les IA peuvent tout faire à votre place, analyser des données plus vite, produire du contenu, automatiser des tâches, quelle est encore votre valeur ajoutée ?

Est-ce que les dirigeants, dont le rôle était souvent d’analyser rapidement les informations et de prendre des décisions froides, vont être remplacés ?

La réponse était plutôt nuancée. Non… sauf pour les entreprises qui refusent de prendre le virage de l’IA. Celles-là risquent effectivement de se faire dépasser.

D’après l’auteur du podcast, les compétences clés pour les prochaines années seraient finalement assez humaines : savoir piloter la technologie avec discernement et savoir diriger des équipes avec une véritable empathie.

Si l’IA devient de plus en plus forte pour expliquer *comment* faire les choses, le rôle du leader devient surtout d’expliquer *pourquoi* on les fait.

En rentrant de ce running, on est passés au potager pour voir si les petits pois et les épinards commençaient à sortir de terre.

Et bonne surprise : les épinards commencent à sortir ! Pour l’instant ce sont de toutes petites pousses. J’espère juste ne pas confondre avec de l’herbe qui pousse…

![3f3ddb01-b08e-4e86-af81-20e4ef28fae2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/genesisledger/EoEq76VxSiFufG5bcSWy9ScthLXj6UaYPfUK6F3HWPhhUS68EybT3mmxkWkELtfGeKL.jpg)

On a aussi récolté un peu de chou kale pour le déjeuner. Si vous pouvez en faire pousser chez vous, ou simplement en acheter, foncez.

Vous lavez les feuilles, vous mettez à peine une cuillère à soupe d’huile d’olive dans une poêle avec de l’ail et du sel, puis vous laissez cuire le tout 10 à 15 minutes.

C’est simple. Et c’est délicieux.

L’après-midi, j’avais une réunion et quelques autres choses à avancer pour le travail.

Bonne journée Hive !

---

title.title: Updates on Hive Roshambo, The 1v1 Rock-Scissor-Paper Mini Game with Real Hive on The Line
title.body: Building [Hive Roshambo](https://hive-roshambo.com) over these last few weeks has been an incredible journey, and I’ve learned so much from everyone who has jumped into the Arena so far. As a solo developer, my goal has always been to create something that feels fast, fun, and deeply integrated into the Hive community we all love. Hive Roshambo is my personal project to bring the classic game of Rock Paper Scissors directly to the Hive blockchain. It’s an on-chain arena where you can challenge friends or strangers to high-stakes (or just for fun) matches, all with the transparency and speed of Hive. You can check it out and start your first match at [hive-roshambo.com](https://hive-roshambo.com). Lately, I've been focusing on the small friction points that can sometimes get in the way of a quick game. That started with how we get into the Arena. While Hive Keychain is fantastic, I wanted to make sure there was always a backup that works across all your devices, so I’ve integrated HiveSigner. It was important to me that whether you're on your phone or at a friend's computer, you have a reliable path to start a match without any setup hurdles.

/> Once I smoothed out the entry, I started thinking about how we share those 'did that really just happen?' moments. Winning a high-stakes match is a rush, and it shouldn't be hard to let your friends know. I’ve added a simple sharing tool that lets you grab a link to your match, either to show off a finished game or to send a direct challenge to a rival. It’s a small addition, but it’s one I’ve been wanting to get right for a while now.

/> Finally, I wanted to make the Arena feel more alive, even when the app is closed. I’ve set up a dedicated bot, `roshambo.app`, to post real-time social notifications. By using comments, every match now creates a small ripple on the blockchain. All of comments has declined rewards by default. It’s my way of making sure that when the Arena is buzzing, the whole Hive ecosystem can see the action.

/>

Thank you for being part of this project. Every match you play and every bit of feedback you send helps me keep building and improving the Arena. I especially want to thank the early testers and the community members who have been sharing their thoughts in the feeds, your support is what keeps me coding late into the night.

See you in the next match.  
  
Check it out: [hive-roshambo.com](https://hive-roshambo.com)

title.title: Should I Add the Gundam Accounts I am Piloting to the Zero List to Help Downvote?
title.body:
![gundam-wing.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hurtlocker/23tkfguoKLFTC1Ks3qbYtMYrQFc1WvqhxpASnkhmFkf3SKasbjcebe6dYLfGZyqWYK7R9.gif)



So some people do not know how the reward pool works.

The reward pool is our common good but it is not a public good. There is a difference!

A common good is basically our shared resource as a \

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hurtlocker/23tGXYmj96MkDGotpinTGFRfj8QAuG4kXXmN8L8dyLYpk1QrfiknjykDVFeMAg5d64JAm.png)

Now obviously Hive is not a community in any traditional framework. We are a bunch of different tribes with a bunch of different agendas.

But all people and bots do have something in common which is the reward pool. This is a shared resource and it is our common good.

A common good is different from a public good because it is not guaranteed. 

A public good is things like the fire department that serves everyone.

A common good is something that we as an ecosystem allocate based on the idea that it will provide long-term value to the ecosystem.

The reward pool is not free money. The reward pool is allocated to you based on the idea that it will improve the ecosystem.

I do not think we treat the reward pool like this right now.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hurtlocker/23tGXYmj96MkDGotpinTGFRfj8QAuG4kXXmN8L8dyLYpk1QrfiknjykDVFeMAg5d64JAm.png)


Right now we treat the reward pool like a public good.

Right now we look at the reward pool and say, \

But this is not true.

It would be very cool if that were true but it is not. Free money does not exist.

If you are getting upvotes it is because people believe you are going to help the ecosystem; in theory anyways.

If you receive downvotes it is because people believe you OR the curator are not good for the ecosystem; in theory anyways. That being said, sometimes downvotes are simply just a disagreement of rewards which I covered in my last post!

If you get downvoted sometimes it means you did nothing wrong. Sometimes it is a disagreement of curation rewards. Sometimes it has nothing to do with you or what you posted. This can be frustrating but also sometimes who knows why you got downvoted? I have been downvoted many times and I do not know why.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hurtlocker/23tGXYmj96MkDGotpinTGFRfj8QAuG4kXXmN8L8dyLYpk1QrfiknjykDVFeMAg5d64JAm.png)


I have been downvoted before. I have been downvoted for who curated me and I have been downvoted for what I curated. That is ok!

Maybe you do not get the max potential curation rewards because of what someone posted or who upvoted it? Maybe you do not get the max author rewards because you got downvoted? That is ok!

The biggest value to Hive is not your rewards or your rating; the biggest value to Hive is it can never be deleted.

This is also a con. What you post is forever. An edited \
does not change that. You can never delete what you what you posted. When you post a \

you can only present the idea that you tried to delete your post; seeing what you originally posted is easy.

So at the end of the day, Hive's reward pool is a common good. At the end of the day, what you posted has been posted!


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/hurtlocker/23tGXYmj96MkDGotpinTGFRfj8QAuG4kXXmN8L8dyLYpk1QrfiknjykDVFeMAg5d64JAm.png)


I created the Gundam accounts because they are fun but also they are a way to contribute to that common good while I get some curation rewards; this is a win win! In my opinions anyways.

I have already been downvoted by one of the accounts that has been upvoted by the manual curators of the Gundam accounts. This is interesting! This is proof that Hive does work.

I think it would be cool if we have the Gundam accounts added to the Zero list to help Downvote and zero out rewards. But I want community feedback.

Your feedback does matter on stuff like this so that is why I am asking.

I did not ask the other Gundam pilots before making this post so for now only these three accounts shown below will be included in my query to you!

Maybe you think the Gundam accounts are weird but I think they are pretty cool 😏

@gundamzerofive

title.title: Challenge #04818-M069: Permission to Ask
title.body:
![jon-handley-P8MXephSELc-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/internutter/23xyXCr6SEWzbXUtyURnP3HLD1P8WtULwFkfujgZvp4sLXG6xndiTzEeNGFxh4HcHqdrp.jpg)

> During court, king Kormwind, tenth of that name, finds himself having a toddler climbing up in his lap and, sucking their thumb, and full of trust, falling asleep. Where are the parents? Near the kitchens exhaustedly trying to handle six other children, most of whom were at that stage of sleepy where they get wilder and grumpy due to being overtired, and trying to figure out where their toddler went. -- Anon Guest

People often thought that only the Nobles lived in their castles. Such was never the case. Nobody who thinks this ever wonders how the castle staff get to work before the Noble in question needs them. For many Nobles, the staff don't count as residents. The phrase \

Not so in Whitekeep.

Kormwind Arachis Felbourne Whitekeep, tenth of his name, and Dex to his friends and family, had a fine example in his father. Kormwind Nine had remembered everyone who crossed his path. He knew their names, their family's names, and had an awareness of their dietary restrictions, health needs, and allergies. To both Dex and his dad alike, the staff were just as much people as anyone else.

Which was why, in the midst of official business in the Grand Court, he knew who the toddler was before they had finished babbling to be picked up. He was also smart enough to check that the kid hadn't soiled themself before he did pick them up.

Dex had kids of his own, and comforted the roaming toddler as if it was the most normal thing in the world.

The Baron venturing her proposal stumbled to a halt in her speech. Staring in shock at what should never happen in a King's court.

The toddler whined and mumbled in Dex's lap.

\
said Dex. To the Baron, he said, \

Transfixed by the sight of a King comforting a child that wasn't his own, the Baron scrambled to resume her speech from where she dropped off. Some in the upper galleries tittered to watch the happening, but the laughter ebbed away as the child curled up and fell asleep.

Dex kept the kid safe in his arms until the Baron's palaver reached its end. Time to pull Dad's favourite trick. \

Stumbling, stuttering, and some wicked cackling from the upper gallery.

_He knew that laugh..._ Dex looked up to find a very familiar set of deep navy horns neighbouring blue-white curls. _Dad_ was visiting.

\

Gently, and very careful not to disturb the sleeping child, he rose from the more ordinary throne of regular business and went to find this child's parents.

They were _supposed_ to be kitchen staff but, as Dex recalled, they had sent in a message saying they were sick. So he found his way to their apartment where it was absolute _bedlam_ within. Six other children - two sets of twins among them - were in various stages of grumpy and sick. Including their otherwise very capable mother. The exasperated father almost fainted in horror at who had their second-youngest child. Only the baby over his shoulder made him brace to stay upright.

\

And while they were making their way to this apartment, Dex would pitch in and help. Starting with depositing his unintended charge into their bed.

These poor souls were even more agog when _Dad_ turned up to help out too. Followed shortly by Mum.

title.title: Yesi Yesi 🇬🇭
title.body:
_ This was my scream when I heard a song I never thought I would ever hear again being played at a party I attended last week. How did the DJ even think of playing that song in an age where new songs are rolling out every second and the old ones are gradually being forgotten as the days pass by?

https://youtu.be/Quvt2giZPjg?si=r5zObVeEx6dfnH3J

I quickly went to YouTube to make a search. I remembered “Yesi Yesi,” and that was all I typed into the search space. The song came up, and it brought back a lot of memories.

It is a Ghanaian song that was released around 2011 or thereabout. We used to play this song on loudspeakers alongside other trending Nigerian songs. I enjoyed hearing the song being played, but sadly, it ended that same period because it wasn't that catchy enough to be kept for long. Yes, it was a banger then, but it faded off as well… maybe it's because it's from Ghana. 😂

* * *

Letter to my Ex by Nasboi and Khaid

https://youtu.be/TvAciKjBFHs?si=YG9HIRRGKwJaxh4U

Nasboi has a way of marketing his songs, and this one isn't an exception, but it came in a different way. Although the whole story of heartbreak looks real because he made different emotional videos, I just knew he was up to something—and this is the song, “Letter to my Ex.”

I haven't paid good attention to it yet. As usual, I was more concerned about his ways of selling his songs.

* * *

Lalala by Young Jonn and Rema

https://youtu.be/SyLoIrE8JAs?si=4WXXlU\_qtUgR3dbT

A good song with two great artists. The kind where just knowing that both of them are on the song makes one want to listen to it by all means.

Thanks for reading.

</center>
</liketuimages>

昨天离开古德寺之后，我就去了一条美食街——山海关路小吃街。我在小红书上查了当地的推荐美食排行榜，排在第一位的是一家叫“李记鸡冠饺”的早餐铺，店里主要卖鸡冠饺和糯米鸡，推荐热度特别高。
 
我当时还在想，热度这么高，味道到底能有多好吃，一定要去尝尝。反正时间很充足，也不用赶路，我就跟着导航往那条街走去。
 
结果还没走到店门口，远远就看到一条长长的队伍。我到的时候是10点50分，既不是早饭时间，也不是中饭时间，队伍居然还能排这么长。
 
好在我观察了一下，队伍前进的速度还比较快，因为老板动作非常利索，一个人大概也就十几二十秒就能点好餐、拿到东西，于是我赶紧站到了队伍后面。
 
站在我前面的是一位正在抽烟的大叔，我连忙后退两步，离他远一点躲烟味。我真的很讨厌被动吸二手烟，对身体不好，而且味道特别呛人。
 
大概排了15分钟多、不到20分钟，终于轮到我了。我本来以为这家网红小店价格会很贵，结果一看，鸡冠饺3块钱一个，糯米鸡也是3块钱一个，和我家楼下早餐店的价格差不多。
 
拿到手的时候还很烫，我迫不及待尝了起来。可能是网红效应和网上吹得太神乎，吃进嘴里感觉也就那样。这家的鸡冠饺，我觉得还没有我们公司楼下旁边那家早餐店的好吃，我还是偏爱皮薄、炸得酥脆，里面包着粉丝、肉和韭菜的鸡冠饺。
 
所以说，网络的宣传力量真的很大，把一样东西说得特别好吃，也许大部分人确实觉得美味，但未必适合自己的口味。不过尝过也不后悔，起码不难吃，只是稍微有点好吃，没有达到我心里的超高预期。我就边走边吃完了这两样小吃，然后前往下一个目的地了。

我的行走路线参考最后一张图哈！

title.title: What are the challenges on route to reach Tanglang La Pass?
title.body:
![image](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/bc85c106e28586aa806ac974666a5d9d0fa664b1f2aa0cb37245e4d4cad8cbd4)



For every passionate motorcyclist, riding through Ladakh is more than just a bucket list item - it’s a rite of passage. And within this rugged Himalayan dream lies Tanglang La, one of the highest motorable mountain passes in the world. Whether you are an Indian adventurer or an Australian thrill-seeker, [Tanglang La Pass](https://www.brahmandtour.com/blog_detail/56/tanglang-la-pass) promises breathtaking beauty, challenging roads, and the kind of experience your Instagram followers will envy for life.

Reaching Tanglang La isn’t your average weekend ride - it’s a full-on Himalayan survival audition. You’ll battle freezing winds, oxygen-starved lungs, unpredictable snow flurries, and roads that look like they were built by mountain goats on strike. Fuel stations? Nope, better carry your own. Mobile network? Cute idea. Add in a very real risk of altitude sickness and the occasional landslide just for fun. But if you can handle the chaos, what waits at the top is pure magic - raw beauty, silent peaks, and the satisfaction of making it where not everyone dares to go. 

You will find limited fuel stations between Tandi and Upshi, so must carry extra fuel. So, it is suggested to acclimatize properly in Leh or Keylong, stay hydrated, and don’t ride like you are in Fast & Furious.



\#tanglangla #highestpassinworld #himalayanpasses #tanglanglapass #lehladakh #motorcycletour #indiamotorcycletour #brahmandtour

Good morning everyone, whenever we talk about a meal prepared for lunch, of course, one that is the most delicious, it is about chicken milanesa, with pumpkin and potato puree. To prepare this milanesa, it is very easy. First, we filet the chicken breast, then we add it to a bowl containing egg, salt to taste, pepper, and parsley, and beat everything well with the meat inside. Then we take it out and coat it with breadcrumbs, and finally fry it in a pan with vegetable fat and oil, resulting in what you see in the photograph.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prm4031/Eou7HC54vwnfRsD8YPVLSU7WyRbmuboGzwqacQCJY7zKJqFNQCyX1b2KBnCnHEHpZNk.png)

For the pumpkin and potato puree, we peeled the potato and cut the pumpkin, then added them to a pot with water. Once boiled and soft, we drained the water and prepared the puree by adding butter, milk, and salt to taste. Honestly, it all turned out very delicious.

Thank you very much for reading and following me.

title.title: The government jointly created measures to prevent charter fraud
title.body:
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPKhMctqs1AgSeUwCaPxfr1xpHMXiTrYS8WHPWqDg7Y6p/image.png)

>A system will be established to help prospective tenants who are about to sign a lease on a deposit basis easily check rights information such as senior deposits at once to avoid lease on a deposit basis.

>Today (10th) the government announced the 'Measures to Prevent Jeonse Fraud' jointly with related ministries such as the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Public Administration and Security.
The government has shifted its policy paradigm, which has been centered on post-rescue measures, to \

focusing on resolving information asymmetry between tenants and landlords and improving the environment for charter transactions transparently, the government explained.

>First of all, we provide integrated information so that prospective tenants can check risk information related to lease contracts, such as senior rights information, before signing a lease contract.
Currently, in order for prospective tenants to obtain senior rights information for rental housing, the process is complicated and inconvenient, such as having to visit a number of government offices with the consent of the lessor before the contract.
In addition, even if all the information was obtained, it was difficult to analyze senior rights relationships such as random checks and diagnose risks.
In particular, it was difficult to check the contract status of individual households because there was only one owner of the entire building and a copy of the register existed only for the entire building.

>In order to solve this inconvenience, the government analyzes senior rights information by linking registration, fixed date, moving-in households, and tax arrears scattered in various institutions, and diagnoses the risk so that prospective tenants can easily check it at once before signing a contract.
To this end, the \

operated by the Housing and Urban Guarantee Corporation (HUG) will be advanced, and all information except registered information, which is public information, will be provided with the consent of the lessor from September.
In addition, the effective timing of the counterforce will be adjusted to 'when processing a transfer report'.
Under the current law, a collateral security takes effect immediately upon receipt, but the counter-power following the tenant's notification of move-in will take effect at midnight the day after receipt.
Some landlords have taken advantage of this time lag to take out mortgage loans just before the tenant's counterattack, and when the building is auctioned off, the loan becomes a senior bond, putting the tenant's deposit down to the next priority.
In order to block the landlord's expediency, the government plans to make an all-out response to the revision of the Housing Lease Protection Act, which calls for raising the timing of tenant opposition to \

pass the National Assembly this month.
In addition, the financial system will be linked so that the bank can check the fixed date and moving-in household information in real time before lending to the lessor to prevent the lessor from making duplicate loans.

>In addition, the duty and responsibility of real estate agents who broker lease contracts will be strengthened.
The real estate agent is obligated to explain the building's rights relationship to the tenant, but the senior data is explained based on the lessor's submission data, which could cause damage to the tenant if the lessor provides inaccurate data.
The government plans to establish an integrated information system that can check rights-related information and give authorized brokers access to it, strengthening their obligation to check the status of senior deposits and explain them to tenants.
If a real estate agent violates his or her duty to check and explain, he or she will raise the level of punishment by raising fines and suspending the business.

> Land, Infrastructure and Transport Minister Kim Yoon-deok said, \

#Jeonse fraud #Real estate #Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport #Lease #Authorized Brokerage #Apartment #Villa
Yonhap News TV Article Statement and Report: Kakaotalk/Linejebo23
Jung Dami smjung@yna.co.kr

For now, a set of measures has been introduced to cover many of the major issues.  

Going forward, tenants should be able to find safer lease agreements by following the procedures outlined above.  

It may still be difficult to stop those who are determined to exploit the system, but at least these steps seem likely to close many of the existing loopholes.

title.title: Damn - it hurts! 👹🍣🎎 My Japan
title.body: ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tvo5JfXVkMeVW26oBNHPSw4qQLXZpg1RhiVqvqDbiEYLqG9nv6aPgNzVeSThQX4iKev.png) [source](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/ouch-speech-bubble-comics-pain-7169962/) As I get older, I inevitably experience more and more aches and pains. Recently, I've been particularly bothered by some pain in my left shoulder and left arm. This isn't a new problem; it probably started a few years ago. But somehow it always got better and I felt fine. However, this time it seems to be more persistent and painful. It was the same last summer, but even then I managed to get rid of the pain with a few exercises and physical activity. But since January things have been different and it seems as if the pain is here to stay. At first, it was just my left upper arm, but now it's mainly my left shoulder, or more precisely, my left shoulder blade. Although I've been doing a few light stretching exercises every morning since the beginning of the year, I can't get rid of the pain. Who knows, maybe it's related to these exercises, although I don't really want to believe that. Shoulder and arm circles are supposed to be exactly the kind of exercises that make this area of the body a little more flexible and smooth. Of course, I had already been to the doctor, but so far he hasn't been able to find anything that could be wrong. Apparently everything is fine and I'm just tense, and he likes to prescribe me some pain patches. Most of the time, I'm then getting a little “rehabilitation,” as physiotherapy is called over here. But ultimately, that just means a few stretching exercises that I can easily do at home. And that's what I do. I always feel that as soon as I do a little exercise, my symptoms get worse. Whether it's weights or a little running, after a short time I somehow feel worse than before. It's not that I have no strength and I'm weak, but it always starts to hurt here and there. Sometimes in my legs and knees, or in my shoulder, which bothers me the most. I'll probably have to go back to the orthopedist, even though I already know exactly what he'll say. He won't be able to find anything wrong this time either, and he'll tell me that with a little “rehabilitation” everything will be fine again soon. Which of course won't be the case, I already know that from my experience. Somehow, I don't know what to do. Finding the right doctor has always been a challenge, and today it seems to have become even more difficult. Actually Japan doesn't have a bad healthcare system, but one of the reasons that keeps me from going back is... ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23zGyvPFmXRvA4HPwwQug65iSBb6TTeF31r3gpM2DSupGbpEoxVg5uUNpXMxCSVJzt17s.png) Somehow, I don't know what to do now. Finding the right doctor has always been a challenge, and today it seems to have become even more difficult. Actully Japan doesn't have a bad healthcare system, but one of the reasons that keeps me from rushing to the doctor is the constant 30% copayment of the total cost. And over time, that can really add up. Well, let's see. Fortunately, it's not like I can't move at all. Most of the time, I'm quite mobile and feel pretty fit. Unfortunately though that wasn't the case this morning, and this painful feeling hasn't gone away since. So what? I'll continue to try to get enough exercise and keep my arm and shoulder from getting rusty. But even though I'd like to sit out the problem and let it heal on its own, it looks like I'll have to see a doctor again. Even though he hasn't been a real help so far, and I don't really have much time right now. But what can you do? Hopefully I still have a few decades ahead of me, and I'd like to enjoy and explore a little more during that time. There's still so much to do! ![blog-ende.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tv6H18WKn98nBVkn2MwVhwWsuFRFgjBGwxLEMVhRZD7zRRbFokaNiAn39fUaB3TxVX6.png)

title.title: My Childhood Food Story: From Spoiled to Simple Living
title.body: > Happy Tuesdayday Hivers! ## When I was seven years old, my aunt, my mother’s sister, took me to live with her because she did not have a daughter. My mother agreed. My aunt’s husband was working abroad, so they were living a fairly comfortable life. Since I was the only girl in the house and the youngest, my aunt spoiled me a lot. She gave me almost everything I wanted. Because of this, I became very picky with food, and it became difficult for my aunt to discipline me. There was a time when I refused to eat unless the dish was hotdog. The bread had to be purple, and the drink had to be orange juice. I refused to eat vegetables and most other foods except the ones I mentioned. Eventually, my aunt became worried that I might get sick because of my unhealthy eating habits, so she decided to bring me back to my real family. When I returned home, I noticed that all my siblings were used to eating vegetables because that was what my parents could afford. One time, I remember crying while eating vegetables, but I still had to eat them because there was a stick beside me, and I would get hit if I refused to eat. Since then, I slowly learned to like vegetables. One of the vegetables I eventually grew to love is spinach. Have you ever tried eating it? ## ![IMG_3319.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23wqnfbsdjGmg3SR6ucciVWK92UBza7ALakeG8auc4rW998aQhmZJzXy43k47gbmLxRoX.jpeg) ## As I grew older, my favorite way to eat spinach was simply steamed, then mixed with calamansi, raw onions, tomatoes, and soy sauce. I’m perfectly happy having that as my main dish. ## ![IMG_3320.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23wgN3sKCQChoxoqgmXi9rbGfMPDhyXRgT437DyHLK94yb9cbviGHzb23nEGzFEZVbzqr.jpeg) ## Before, we used to grow a lot of spinach, but a storm destroyed most of our plants. Last February, we were able to get new seedlings, so we transferred them into plastic bags filled with good soil. Spinach is actually very easy to grow and doesn’t require much care, so it grows quickly. ## ![IMG_3321.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23wCA67mSB7w9JJTHw2hSAekZ9f1eSLh3XSxemcTqw58AHnbCm8C48MCY1NuWjS2Mr6T5.jpeg) ## ## ![IMG_3322.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23wMaNVXdD4vLGDVLWw37LMEGqxrwSiZx4i711gX2zA15EuQ5dzoCYM9eNQYUqVcRZZ7e.jpeg) ## ![IMG_3355.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23uFTQiH11p3VRTTV9Ce3Aqn1btBXKCPGHJvrbyEh7TwCMLP4RUBsXpPh16ioNCbTMu8F.jpeg) ## Yesterday, this is how big the plants have become. They were planted on February 16, and now they are already very healthy. My mother transferred them near the base of our malunggay tree so they can climb and spread there. ## ![IMG_3492.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23vsLXiNXuJ6WbvLXta3tv4DGTprTYLsHbNCMQEeTbd4avRHBKiWex34dYcDCNHHoJv8e.jpeg) ## Food has become very expensive nowadays, and it’s really better to grow your own vegetables if you can. It truly helps you save money. ##

title.title: Bringing zero fee commerce to local businesses
title.body:
Hello Hive community!

![post4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/innopay/246b2pw9VDitPABb2di8nvLfQ6X9J25N7pYWzNZ6dLGsxBmA2vkobHjS2MFsy7Za3NSao.png)

We talked a lot about cutting out legacy middlemen and bringing zero-fee transactions to European merchants. But today, as builders, we need to be completely honest about the biggest roadblock to mass Web3 adoption at the retail level.

**The Volatility Problem**

We all love the idea of paying for our morning coffee with crypto. But put yourself in the shoes of a local cafe owner in Europe. Their rent, their suppliers, and their employee wages are all fixed costs. If they accept a volatile cryptocurrency for a €4 coffee, and the market dips 10% by the end of the day, that merchant just lost their entire profit margin.
This is why, despite years of hype, most local businesses still refuse to integrate decentralized payments. The risk is simply too high.

**The Missing Link: Hive Backed Dollars (HBD)**

This exact problem is why Innopay is building on the Hive ecosystem. To get local European businesses to actually use a blockchain, they need a stable unit of account.

We aren't asking a bakery to gamble on market charts; we are providing them with the stability of Hive Backed Dollars (HBD). By utilizing HBD on the backend of the Innopay ecosystem, we bridge the gap between Web3 ideals and Web2 realities:

1. **Predictability:** The merchant knows that the value they receive at the checkout counter is the value they will actually hold at the end of the week.
2. **True Decentralization:** Unlike centralized stablecoins that can be frozen by corporate issuers, HBD offers a decentralized, community-backed alternative.
3. **Seamless Bridging:** The end-user gets a frictionless payment experience, and the merchant gets stable, usable value without the anxiety of a bad market day.

**Theory Into Practice: Bringing Real Fiat to Hive**

But Innopay isn't just a theoretical concept. We provide a valuable service in the real world right now, allowing both customers and merchants to save time at checkout while bypassing banking fees.

More importantly for this community, this service actively brings fiat money into the Hive ecosystem.

Just this morning, a healthy batch of fiat revenue from daily sales was used to buy Hive, withdrawn to the blockchain, and turned into HBD to be reused as a means of payment. Where did this money come from? It came from everyday people ordering food and drinks at Indie's, one of our local partner restaurants here in Luxembourg.

If we want Web3 to replace traditional credit card networks, we have to offer a product that is objectively better and safer for the business owner. HBD is the tool that allows us to do exactly that.

Here is the ultimate proof that Web3 can beat traditional banking: Indie's actually finds it more profitable to keep this revenue staked in HBD to capture its native blockchain yield, rather than letting it sit as depreciating euros in a traditional bank account. **Real Adoption Requires Real Utility.**

What are the processing fees like in your local area? Do business owners complain about the cost of accepting cards? Let’s discuss it in the comments!

title.body:
Hello bestie, happy new month from me to you as this is my first post for the month. Also, Trust your week is going well, fruitful and productive. God bless you. So today I will tell you how I had my semo-buns, but before that, there is a story that led to it. 
One of the days, while I was still in university, I got home and was so hungry, tired, and low on cash, as at that time, I also did not have foodstuffs to quickly prepare a meal to eat. So I checked what I had at home, and I saw a small bottle of oil, semovita, and seasoning. Then I had the thought of making something out of the semovita, be it puff puff or pancake. At that time, I felt I should do something to satisfy my hunger, so I mixed it all and fried it. Guess what? It was so nice, and it tasted like puff puff. Ever since then, I started making it as snacks to eat anytime I feel like eating, but I decided to do it a different way this time and that is making it in a buns form.

![6B3F964F-955F-4205-A012-6FD87829C9BB.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23zbHNvZt3Jr7cwmpBhK8c2VeJMf7d1WQnPtiH6Pj9USziSGoTmdZ4hFVws23xwigimeg.jpeg)

 
**Materials used**
Semotiva 
Sugar
Milk
Salt
Egg
Water
Vegetable oil
I poured my desired quantity of semovita into a bowl, added my milk, salt,, and a little sugar, and yes little sugar, because I was still going to add more to my egg. 

![E38C8172-82A4-4882-B7C1-40D3F851E367.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23uQpegVPxPxTToHSbyrggi7weKitZeH7n5RLaWgJxnQouK5MVbtDyiFjKDZqEdVWumvJ.jpeg)

I broke my egg into another plate, added sugar to it, and whisked it till it was smooth. After that, I poured a little water into my semovita mixed with a pinch of salt and sugar and mixed evenly. Thereafter, I added my egg to it, but I noticed it was not easy to mix using my hands because it was already having lumps, so I had to take time and mix properly. Although I had the thought to pour my egg into the semovita before and water when next I would do it.

![79A9F0F7-17C1-4B52-A0DC-CAD93F6EA9FA.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23wMW1QFnKs86kDDXJBjvbRPoXgonNvhRebYSFMmQ4vWmEEcREHZYNFzSkBvZppxyWtjF.jpeg)

![749F4EAA-BCF4-476C-A0C6-36C397FB36BE.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23xKp7cMVEVtiBufHJAkmnN3MaTxry9E1rEDiK8NXGdKqNnzG1R5p8GtJRoiE9xSnD7eT.jpeg)

At this point, my dough is ready for frying, so I used a small spoon to scoop it so as to get the buns effect, and my semo buns are ready. The taste was so great.
- 
![95884F9C-8D1E-498C-9E5C-54753BAF683E.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23uQnVH18x6B8KDjj9ngias5QkmcV2Kg8DzHr5RmcrjddraNc7Kma93y28XZCLFkJEkV8.jpeg)

![2C79C81D-1504-4E41-AF7E-197F91815E1C.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seun-thegg/23wMU4gwYQ1DN14Jdi3EvuGgjVhMNjSpVPkkuEZuK6n6Es4xW4tZWcnrHeSttxWsFTnmf.jpeg)

Thanks for your time, and I would love to know in the comment section if you will be trying it out.

title.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![8DFizIGcR7d7a9iH_IMG_20260310_073337.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/8DFizIGcR7d7a9iH_IMG_20260310_073337/8DFizIGcR7d7a9iH_IMG_20260310_073337.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

没有动态的日子，都在安心静养。
大门不出，二门不迈，日子平淡无波澜，也就没什么特别可记录。
安安静静在家，把身体慢慢养好。
 
今天3月10号，是发工资的日子。
快四点了，工资还没到账。
虽然收入微薄，撑不起生活重担，当个零花钱也算一点慰藉。
可一旦没了业务，单靠这点薪资，真的太难生存。
 
前不久，大区一位去年才入职的同事离职了。
市场环境不好，业务难做，
一个月一千左右的薪资，连自己都难顾全，更别提养家养孩子。
 
今年三八节，公司安安静静，一点动静都没有。
往年还有大牌护肤品、彩妆，
去年至少还有蕉下防晒套装——伞、帽子、包包，很是贴心。
今年半天假没有、礼没有，连一句通知都没有。
 
心里明白，大环境不好、公司效益不佳，都能理解。
可越是这样，人反而越容易少了几分斗志。
 
不知道别的行业是不是也这般冷清。
连教育都如此萧条，其他行业大概也差不多。
只是偶尔会忍不住想：
连教育都这般收紧，那些资源与力气，又会流向哪里呢？
 
日子难，但还在过。
先养好自己，再慢慢等风来。

title.title: Why Mirrors Feel Unsettling in Horror Games
title.body:
Mirrors are ordinary objects. You see them every day without thinking twice.

In most video games, they barely matter at all. Sometimes they’re decorative, sometimes they reflect the environment poorly, and sometimes they’re not reflective at all.

But in [horror games](https://horrorgamesfree.com), mirrors suddenly feel important.

You pass one hanging on a wall or standing in a dark bathroom, and your attention lingers. You slow down slightly. Maybe you even stop moving for a moment.

Not because anything has happened.

Because something might.

Mirrors Show More Than the Player

In horror games, mirrors introduce a strange possibility: they can show things the player cannot see directly.

You might glance at the reflection to check what’s behind your character. The room appears familiar, but the reflection adds a new layer of perspective.

Suddenly you’re not just looking forward anymore.

You’re watching the space behind you at the same time.

That extra perspective feels useful, but it also feels risky. If something appears in the reflection that isn’t visible in the room itself, the player notices instantly.

And the brain reacts before logic has time to catch up.

Did something just move back there?

Reflections Create Doubt

Mirrors introduce a subtle problem: reflections are easy to misinterpret.

Lighting might distort shapes. Shadows shift differently in reflections than they do in direct view. Objects can look unfamiliar when reversed.

These small distortions encourage doubt.

Maybe that dark shape behind your character is just a chair. Maybe the flicker in the mirror is only a lighting effect.

But maybe it isn’t.

Because horror games thrive on uncertainty, reflections become perfect tools for planting small questions in the player’s mind.

Even when nothing is happening, mirrors create the feeling that something could be wrong.

Players Expect Something to Appear

The longer you play horror games, the more you start anticipating certain moments.

Mirrors are one of them.

Players have learned through experience that reflections sometimes reveal unexpected things: a figure standing behind you, a shadow that wasn’t there before, or something that disappears when you turn around.

Because of that expectation, mirrors feel tense even when they’re harmless.

You approach slowly. You glance at the reflection. You check behind you just to be sure.

Most of the time, nothing happens.

But the expectation alone changes how the player behaves.

Mirrors Turn the Camera Around

Another reason mirrors feel uncomfortable is that they force the player to confront their own character.

In many games, you rarely see your character’s face. The camera focuses on the world ahead, not the person moving through it.

Mirrors interrupt that habit.

Suddenly your character is staring back at you. The lighting might make them look tired or eerie. Their expression might seem strangely blank.

This moment can feel oddly personal.

Instead of observing the environment, you’re observing yourself inside the environment.

And in horror settings, that reflection can feel slightly wrong—even if nothing about it has actually changed.

The Bathroom Mirror Problem

Bathrooms are one of the most common places players encounter mirrors in horror games.

There’s a reason for that.

Bathrooms tend to be small, enclosed spaces. The lighting is often harsh or uneven. The mirror usually sits directly in front of the player, forcing them to look at it.

These environments create a perfect setup for tension.

You step inside. The room feels quiet. The mirror shows the entire space behind you.

Players often check the reflection instinctively before leaving the room.

Not because the game asked them to.

Because horror has trained them to expect surprises there.

Reflections Can Hide Information

Sometimes mirrors in horror games reveal things players would otherwise miss.

A hidden message written behind the player. A figure standing somewhere outside the camera’s field of view. An environmental detail that only appears from the reflected angle.

These moments reward careful observation.

Players start studying reflections more closely, scanning them the same way they scan dark corners or distant hallways.

This behavior adds another layer of exploration.

The mirror isn’t just decoration—it’s a second window into the environment.

When Mirrors Break the Rules

Occasionally, horror games take mirrors one step further.

The reflection doesn’t behave normally.

Your character moves, but the reflection hesitates. Something appears behind you that disappears when you turn around. The reflection shows a different version of the room entirely.

Moments like these are deeply unsettling because they violate a basic expectation.

Mirrors are supposed to be reliable. They reflect reality exactly as it is.

When that rule breaks, the world itself feels unstable.

Players begin questioning what’s real in the environment.

And once that doubt appears, it spreads.

Mirrors Slow Players Down

Like many subtle horror elements, mirrors change pacing.

Instead of rushing through rooms, players slow down to check reflections. They turn the camera slightly, watching how the mirrored space reacts.

These small pauses stretch the moment.

The player spends longer in an otherwise ordinary room, simply because the mirror invites curiosity—and a bit of caution.

For people interested in how visual details influence player behavior, exploring \[environmental design in horror games\] shows how even simple objects like mirrors can guide attention and shape tension.

The trick isn’t always adding monsters.

Sometimes it’s just giving players something to watch.

The Fear of Seeing Something

At the core of the mirror’s power in horror games is a simple idea: players are afraid of seeing something unexpected.

Not necessarily something attacking them.

Just something there.

A figure that wasn’t present a moment ago. A movement in the background. A reflection that reveals the presence of another character.

The mirror doesn’t create the threat.

It reveals it.

And revelation is often scarier than the threat itself.

title.title: Building Or Destroying. #Shadow Hunters Contest 416
title.body:
When I was younger, my grand parents usually told us the tales of how they suffered and were in pains during the times of war. I would not want to witness such judging by what I heard from them. I have heard about the first world war, the second world war and even the Nigerian civil war. All of these were not interesting scenarios. So, why are we still nursing war tones all over the world? Can't we coexist peacefully? I think that the all thing about all these wars is not going to land us in something palatable. Let there be no wars.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZroJxK5YXfZGMXHg85CCaHXMQHxDYSmetFBr5YmKXAcp/1773129183065.jpg)

Presently, there are wars in different forms all over the place. Where there is no full fleshed war, terrorism militants activities subject people to untold hardship. Why? Why are we allowing this evil in our midst this much? Please let's stop destroying the world. Everytime there is war, we are destroying rather than building. We should gather our resources together and join our hands to build rather than to destroy. Let the destruction stop; let us join hands together to build.

Those who have nuclear resources can use them in the manner that they will profit the world rather than destroying it. Building is better than destroying. Let us consider the generations of our children coming. It is not time to destroy the world; we should rather build.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQj9Y76EezEfhZz4fAxp8abFTwyqrwLPUN5VPnQfyLdj4/1773129294116.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXvCyUhVJjQ6xu2kc6txErrb1AuxJM3tu1HhQ8PWCkRKm/1773129294962.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYm6DfswoRQraYDjJCq7vE5egexCubL8T5gjpB7EAGqVV/1773129295797.jpg)

It is my pleasure coming your way again today. Join me in the #smash contest round 416. Have a great week.😊

title.title: Cuidando su proceder los que saben siempre podrán mejor actuar (Poesía) [ESP/ENG] By taking care of their actions, those who know will always be able to act better
title.body:
Incertidumbre que en el camino amilana a millones
Dolores de parto que parecen nunca cesar angustiando corazones
Delirios de quienes no entienden lo que no quieren entender
Premoniciones de quienes saben que todo debe cambiar y suceder.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUoqEEE2AMw7s1AMu8c2YvpmdzAzDqToTePx1bv54QzyZ/image.png)
[Origen de la imagen](https://pixabay.com/photos/depression-man-anger-sadness-2912404/)

Los trazos están dados y la suerte está echada en el camino cierto
Vientos que soplan y una luz ilumina el rostro de los pocos elegidos
Cada mente es un mundo que suspira en silencio y esquiva el olvido
Los precavidos saben que la sabiduría y prudencia es su mayor valentía.

Los suspiros y lamentos se entremezclan por igual en la espesa amargura
La esperanza de quienes saben que la vida fue injusta, pero debe mejorar
Los que trabajan duro día tras día y no cesan su empeño por crecer, vigilan
Las experiencias tristes no deben determinar el futuro, y eso se ha de entender.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYiYBrybxvWoxk4eXpJUzwJ9jUmTj6HLyd2LcsCsNH1Gy/image.png)
[Origen de la imagen](https://pixabay.com/photos/face-tears-sadness-warrior-weeping-1271161/)

Los cambios que se auguran traen esperanzas pero también miles de incógnitas
Cánticos se oyen de quienes ilusamente se quieren emocionar antes de tiempo
El futuro es promisorio, pero aún no ha llegado y cuidado hay que tener
Los pollos no se cuentan antes de tiempo, eso es un viejo adagio que ha de prevalecer.

Me acuesto en una hamaca y pienso y pienso hasta que me duermo
Las horas pasan y me vuelvo a levantar entre hondas reflexiones
Veo las nubes y siento el viento soplar en mi cara desnuda
Veo a muchos queriendo inútilmente que todos dejen de pensar.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT5w8JiGnmHn3gzLrBQ1vZhS84a6oWD4rkGNEri2tRJ1C/image.png)
[Origen de la imagen](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-depressed-sad-loneliness-male-3959784/)

La mente de los piensan con claridad es un tesoro
Es un valor temido por muchos y anhelado por otros
Sin pensamiento lúcido no hay decisión ni acción, eso hay saberlo
La precisión de los sabios es lo que los necios y malvados temen en su celo.

Entre parajes de eterna locura se han de mover los prudentes
Entre miles de necios tendrán que defender la cordura de sus mentes
Manteniendo la serenidad los sabios podrán su inteligencia cuidar
Cuidando su proceder los que saben siempre podrán mejor actuar.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWpSJSxMiaSn3eNn8dGXkYZPmHW7LknPGXHDcp5ctYSXr/image.png)
[Origen de la imagen](https://pixabay.com/photos/woman-snow-winter-portrait-578429/)

La situación de un mundo que se vuelve oscuro por momentos
La claridad despierta que vive en nosotros nos hace siempre reflexionar
Somos comedidos si le damos la oportunidad a nuestra sabiduría interior
Somos los garantes de que nuestros pasos siempre sean los mejores y lo más certeros.

Cuando la soledad parece llegar a los corazones de muchos es cuando duele
Pero cuando la noche parece más oscura es cuando finalmente amanece
Las intrigas de quienes atormentaron a tantos están languideciendo lentamente
Lo que por tanto tiempo fue, ya pronto será un triste recuerdo a olvidar.

Soñar sinceramente con un mundo mejor es la meta de los bienaventurados
Los ególatras e hipócritas no prevalecerán en un mundo de bienestar honesto
La vida trae sorpresas positivas a los buenos, y lecciones indescriptibles a los malvados
Parece que entre dolores y placeres siempre vivirá el ser humano.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQQTjrQkG4VKgTsFJQgSxVeRmWU2pESKd2tjJd29aS3aB/image.png)
[Origen de la imagen](https://pixabay.com/photos/girl-lavenders-flowers-model-1472185/)

Se oye una voz que dice \

Lo que se anhela largamente una vez conseguido se cuida mucho más
Dichosos los llamados a ver estos nuevos tiempos y a vivirlos y disfrutarlos
La serenidad, la bondad y la justicia serán siempre las metas a proteger y mantener.

Nunca ceses de tener pensamientos buenos y sinceros
La mente de los justos y sabios siempre será lo más bello
Ser diametralmente opuesto a las masas impensantes es lo correcto
La plenitud que se alcanza al ser autónomos de pensamiento es eterna.

**Poema escrito por el puño y letra de @poetisotizo.**
**Espero les haya gustado.**

_________
### English version
_________

Uncertainty that frightens millions along the way
Labor pains that seem to never end, distress the hearts
Delusions of those who don't understand what they don't want to understand
Premonitions of those who know that everything must change and come to pass.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUoqEEE2AMw7s1AMu8c2YvpmdzAzDqToTePx1bv54QzyZ/image.png)
[Image source](https://pixabay.com/photos/depression-man-anger-sadness-2912404/)

The course is set and fate is sealed on the certain path
Winds blow and a light illuminates the faces of the chosen few
Each mind is a world that sighs in silence and avoids oblivion
The cautious know that wisdom and prudence are their greatest courage.

Sighs and laments mingle equally in the thick bitterness
The hope of those who know that life has been unfair, but must improve
Those who work hard day after day and never cease their efforts to grow, watch
Sad experiences should not determine the future, and that must be understood.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYiYBrybxvWoxk4eXpJUzwJ9jUmTj6HLyd2LcsCsNH1Gy/image.png)
[Image source](https://pixabay.com/photos/face-tears-sadness-warrior-weeping-1271161/)

The changes that are predicted bring hope, but also thousands of unknowns
Songs are heard from those who naively want to get excited prematurely
The future is promising, but it hasn't arrived yet, and we must be careful
Don't count your chickens before they hatch; that's an old adage that must prevail.

I lie down in a hammock and think and think until I fall asleep
The hours pass, and I wake up again deep in thought
I see the clouds and feel the wind blow on my bare face
I see many trying in vain to make everyone stop thinking.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT5w8JiGnmHn3gzLrBQ1vZhS84a6oWD4rkGNEri2tRJ1C/image.png)
[Image source](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-depressed-sad-loneliness-male-3959784/)

The mind of those who think clearly is a treasure
It's a value feared by many and longed for by others
Without lucid thought, there is no decision or action; that's something to know
The precision of the wise is what the foolish and wicked fear in their jealousy.

Among places of eternal madness, the prudent must move
Among thousands of fools, they will have to defend the sanity of their minds
Maintaining serenity, the wise will be able to safeguard their intelligence
By taking care of their actions, those who know will always be able to act better.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWpSJSxMiaSn3eNn8dGXkYZPmHW7LknPGXHDcp5ctYSXr/image.png)
[Image source](https://pixabay.com/photos/woman-snow-winter-portrait-578429/)

The situation of a world that grows dark at times
The awakened clarity that lives within us always makes us reflect
We are measured if we give our inner wisdom a chance
We are the guarantors that our steps will always be the best and most certain.

When loneliness seems to reach the hearts of many, that is when it hurts
But when the night seems darkest, that is when dawn finally breaks
The intrigues of those who tormented so many are slowly fading away
What was for so long will soon be a sad memory to be forgotten.

To sincerely dream of a better world is the goal of the blessed
Egomaniacs and hypocrites will not prevail in a world of honest well-being
Life brings positive surprises to the good, and indescribable lessons to the wicked
It seems that humanity will always live amidst pain and pleasure.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQQTjrQkG4VKgTsFJQgSxVeRmWU2pESKd2tjJd29aS3aB/image.png)
[Image source](https://pixabay.com/photos/girl-lavenders-flowers-model-1472185/)

A voice is heard saying, \

What is longed for, once attained, is cherished even more
Blessed are those called to see these new times and to live and enjoy them
Serenity, kindness, and justice will always be the goals to protect and uphold.

Never cease to have good and sincere thoughts
The minds of the just and wise will always be the most beautiful
Being diametrically opposed to the unthinking masses is the right thing to do
The fulfillment achieved by being autonomous in thought is eternal.

**Poem written by the hand of @poetisotizo.**
**I hope you liked it.**

# Learn Python Series (#53) - Deployment & Production Best Practices

Your API works on localhost. Tests pass. Authentication is solid. You're feeling good.

Then you deploy, and everything falls apart. Database connections time out under load. One slow external API call blocks all your workers. Logs are a wall of unstructured text that tells you nothing useful. A server crashes at 3 AM and nobody notices until users complain hours later.

The gap between \

is where most developers get humbled — including me, more than once ;-). This episode is about closing that gap systematically.

**Nota bene:** Deployment is the _easy_ part. A `docker push` and you're live. _Staying live_ — that's the real skill. Monitoring, logging, graceful degradation, connection pooling, knowing what to do when things break at scale. This is what separates hobbyist projects from production systems, and it's what we'll dig into today.

## Development vs Production Servers — Why It Matters

During development, you run Uvicorn directly:

```bash
uvicorn main:app --reload
```

The `--reload` flag watches for file changes and restarts the server automatically. Convenient for development. But here's what `--reload` actually does under the hood: it uses file system watchers (watchfiles on Linux, fsevents on macOS) to detect changes, then **kills the running process and spawns a new one**. Every active connection is dropped. Every in-flight request is abandoned. In development, that's a mild annoyance. In production, that's users getting 502 errors.

More importantly, a single Uvicorn process means a single Python event loop, which means a single point of failure. If that process crashes, your API is down — completely, instantly, silently (unless you've set up monitoring, which is the other half of this episode).

**Production** uses a process manager:

```bash
gunicorn main:app \
    --workers 4 \
    --worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker \
    --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 \
    --access-logfile - \
    --error-logfile -
```

Why **Gunicorn + Uvicorn**? Gunicorn is a mature, battle-tested process manager. It handles spawning workers, monitoring their health, restarting crashed workers, and distributing incoming connections. Uvicorn (via `UvicornWorker`) handles the actual async request processing within each worker. Together they give you: process supervision, graceful restarts, and horizontal scaling within a single machine.

## Worker Count — The Formula and the Nuance

The standard formula is:

```
workers = (2 × CPU cores) + 1
```

For a 4-core machine: `(2 × 4) + 1 = 9` workers. The reasoning: during I/O operations (database queries, external API calls, file reads), the worker is waiting — not computing. Having more workers than cores ensures CPUs stay busy while other workers are blocked on I/O.

But this formula has limits. Each worker is a **separate OS process** that loads the entire application into memory. A FastAPI app with SQLAlchemy, Pydantic models, and imported packages might use 50-150MB per worker. Nine workers = 450MB-1.3GB just for the application layer.

For **CPU-bound** workloads (image processing, heavy computation), use `cores + 1`. For **I/O-bound** workloads (most web APIs), `(2 × cores) + 1` is the right starting point. But always profile — theory is no substitute for measuring actual memory usage and response times under realistic load:

```bash
# Check memory per worker
ps aux | grep gunicorn | awk '{print $6/1024 \

, $0}'
```

## Environment Configuration with pydantic-settings

Never hardcode configuration. Not \

— _never_:

```python
# settings.py
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings
from functools import lru_cache

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    database_url: str
    secret_key: str
    debug: bool = False
    allowed_origins: list[str] = [\

# Worker config
    workers: int = 4
    db_pool_size: int = 10
    db_max_overflow: int = 20

    model_config = {\

}

@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

The `@lru_cache` ensures settings are loaded once and reused. In development, create a `.env` file:

```bash
# .env (NEVER commit this to git — add to .gitignore)
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost/mydb
SECRET_KEY=dev-only-change-in-production
DEBUG=True
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
```

In production, set environment variables directly — via Docker, systemd, your cloud provider's secret manager, or whatever your infrastructure uses. The point is: **the same code runs everywhere**, only the configuration changes.

Using `pydantic-settings` instead of raw `os.getenv()` gives you type validation at startup. If `DATABASE_URL` is missing or `DB_POOL_SIZE` isn't an integer, the application fails immediately with a clear error — not thirty minutes later when the first database query runs and you get a cryptic traceback.

```python
# In your FastAPI app
from fastapi import Depends

app = FastAPI()

@app.get(\

: settings.workers}
```

## Health Check Endpoints — Simple and Deep

Load balancers, container orchestrators (Kubernetes), and monitoring tools need to know if your app is healthy. Two levels of health checks:

**Liveness** — \

(should traffic be routed here?):

```python
from sqlalchemy import text

@app.get(\

— maybe the database is temporarily down and will recover. Kubernetes uses these differently, and getting it wrong causes cascading restarts that make outages worse.

## Graceful Shutdown — Finish What You Started

When Gunicorn restarts a worker (deploy, scale-down, crash recovery), it sends **SIGTERM**. The worker should finish its current requests before exiting:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Startup
    logger.info(\

)
    # Initialize connection pools, caches, background tasks
    yield
    # Shutdown
    logger.info(\

)
    # Close database pools, flush logs, cancel background tasks

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
```

FastAPI's **lifespan** context manager (replacing the old `on_event(\

)` pattern) runs code before the first request and after the last request. This is where you initialize and clean up shared resources — database connection pools, Redis clients, HTTP client sessions.

Gunicorn's `--graceful-timeout 30` gives workers 30 seconds to finish in-flight requests after receiving SIGTERM. If they don't finish in time, SIGKILL ends them forcefully. Set this high enough for your slowest expected request, but not so high that deploys take forever.

## Structured Logging — JSON or Go Home

In development, human-readable logs are fine:

```
2026-02-23 14:30:22 - INFO - User alice@example.com logged in
```

In production, you need **structured** (JSON) logs that log aggregation tools can parse, index, and query:

```python
import logging
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone

class JSONFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record):
        log_entry = {
            \

):
    handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    handler.setFormatter(JSONFormatter())
    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers.clear()
    root.addHandler(handler)
    root.setLevel(getattr(logging, level.upper()))
```

The `request_id` field is critical for production debugging. Add a unique ID to every request using middleware:

```python
import uuid

@app.middleware(\

)
async def add_request_id(request, call_next):
    request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    request.state.request_id = request_id
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers[\

] = request_id
    return response
```

When a user reports \

they give you the request ID from the response header, and you can grep your logs for every event related to that specific request. Without request IDs, debugging production issues in a multi-worker, multi-instance system is like finding a needle in a haystack — while the haystack is on fire.

## Database Connection Pooling — Don't Create Connections Per Request

Every database connection involves a TCP handshake, authentication, and protocol negotiation. On a fast network that's ~5ms. At 100 requests/second, that's 500ms of pure overhead every second — just connecting.

**Connection pooling** maintains a set of open connections that get reused:

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine

engine = create_engine(
    settings.database_url,
    pool_size=10,           # Keep 10 connections alive
    max_overflow=20,        # Allow 20 more under burst load
    pool_pre_ping=True,     # Check connection health before use
    pool_recycle=3600,      # Recreate connections after 1 hour
    pool_timeout=30,        # Wait max 30s for a connection from pool
)
```

`pool_pre_ping=True` sends a lightweight query (`SELECT 1`) before handing a connection to your code. This catches stale connections (database restarted, network timeout) before they cause a cryptic \
error mid-query. The cost is one extra round-trip per checkout — worth it for the reliability.\n\n`pool_recycle=3600` prevents the \

problem. Many databases (and firewalls in between) silently drop connections after a timeout. Recycling forces reconnection before that happens.

**Sizing the pool**: `pool_size` should roughly match your worker count. Each worker handles one request at a time (in the synchronous path), so one connection per worker is the baseline. `max_overflow` handles burst traffic — these extra connections are created on demand and destroyed when returned to the pool.

## Docker Deployment — Multi-Stage Builds

A production Dockerfile should be small, reproducible, and secure:

```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build dependencies
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /build
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --user --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Stage 2: Runtime
FROM python:3.11-slim

# Don't run as root
RUN useradd --create-home appuser
USER appuser
WORKDIR /home/appuser/app

# Copy installed packages from builder
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /home/appuser/.local
ENV PATH=/home/appuser/.local/bin:$PATH

# Copy application code
COPY --chown=appuser:appuser . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD [\

]
```

Key points: the multi-stage build keeps your final image small (no compiler toolchains, no pip cache). The `appuser` prevents the container from running as root — a basic security requirement. `--no-cache-dir` avoids storing pip's download cache in the image.

For a complete local setup with a database, use **docker-compose**:

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - \

env_file: .env
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: myuser
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: mypassword
      POSTGRES_DB: mydb
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: [\

]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

The `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` ensures the API doesn't start until PostgreSQL is actually accepting connections — not just when the container is running (the container starts before the database process is ready, which is a classic race condition).

## Common Production Pitfalls — Learn from Others' Mistakes

### No Request Timeouts

Without timeouts, a slow external API can hold your workers hostage indefinitely:

```python
import httpx

# WRONG — hangs forever if the external service is down
response = await client.get(\

)
async def list_users(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    users = db.query(User).all()  # synchronous call in async context!
    return users
```

When you declare an endpoint with `async def`, FastAPI runs it on the asyncio event loop. A synchronous database call (`db.query(...)`) blocks that event loop — no other request can be processed until the query completes. With standard SQLAlchemy, either use `def` (not `async def`) so FastAPI runs it in a threadpool automatically, or use **async SQLAlchemy**:

```python
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncSession

async_engine = create_async_engine(
    \

)
async def list_users(db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_db)):
    result = await db.execute(select(User))
    return result.scalars().all()  # truly non-blocking
```

### Missing Database Indexes

The difference between indexed and unindexed lookups on a million-row table can be 1ms vs 2000ms:

```python
# Model definition — always index columns you filter or join on
class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = \

id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    email = Column(String, unique=True, index=True)      # filtered in login
    created_at = Column(DateTime, index=True)             # filtered in reports
    role = Column(String, index=True)                     # filtered in admin views
```

Rule of thumb: if you `WHERE` on it, `ORDER BY` it, or `JOIN` on it — index it. The write-time cost of maintaining indexes is almost always worth the read-time savings.

### Database Migration Strategy

Never modify production schemas by hand. Use **Alembic** (which we introduced in episode #51):

```bash
# Generate migration from model changes
alembic revision --autogenerate -m \

# Apply in production
alembic upgrade head
```

Always review autogenerated migrations before applying. Alembic doesn't detect everything (renamed columns look like a drop + add), and destructive operations need manual verification.

Run migrations **before** deploying new code that expects the new schema. The sequence is: migrate → deploy → verify. Never the other way around — new code hitting an old schema produces errors under load.

## Monitoring — Know Before Your Users Do

The four golden signals of monitoring (per Google's SRE book):

| Signal | What it tells you | How to measure |
|--------|-------------------|----------------|
| **Latency** | How long requests take | p50, p95, p99 response times |
| **Traffic** | How much demand you're handling | Requests per second |
| **Errors** | What's failing | 4xx and 5xx response rates |
| **Saturation** | How close to capacity you are | CPU, memory, connection pool usage |

A simple middleware to track request metrics:

```python
import time

@app.middleware(\

)
async def metrics_middleware(request, call_next):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    duration = time.perf_counter() - start

    logger.info(
        \

: round(duration * 1000, 2),
        }
    )
    return response
```

For serious production monitoring, integrate with **Prometheus** (metrics collection) + **Grafana** (dashboards). The `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` package adds standard HTTP metrics with one line:

```python
from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator

Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app)
# Now /metrics endpoint serves Prometheus-format metrics
```

Set up alerts for: error rate > 1%, p99 latency > 2 seconds, CPU > 80% sustained, database connection pool > 90% utilization. These thresholds catch problems before users notice them.

## What to remember from this one

In this episode, we covered the full deployment lifecycle:

- **Gunicorn + Uvicorn** provides process management, worker supervision, and graceful restarts that raw Uvicorn alone cannot
- **Worker count** `(2 × cores) + 1` balances CPU and I/O, but always profile memory usage under realistic load
- **pydantic-settings** validates configuration at startup — fail fast, not at 3 AM when the first edge case hits
- **Liveness vs readiness** health checks serve different purposes — getting this wrong causes cascading failures
- **Lifespan context managers** replace the old startup/shutdown events for resource management
- **Structured JSON logging** with request IDs makes production debugging tractable instead of hopeless
- **Connection pooling** with `pool_pre_ping` and `pool_recycle` prevents stale connections from causing mysterious errors
- **Multi-stage Docker builds** with non-root users produce small, secure images
- **docker-compose** with health check conditions prevents startup race conditions
- **Request timeouts** on external calls prevent worker starvation
- **async def + sync DB = blocked event loop** — use `def` endpoints or async database drivers
- **Index every column** you filter, sort, or join on
- **Migrate before deploying**, never after — and always review autogenerated migrations
- **Four golden signals**: latency, traffic, errors, saturation — know them before your users do

We've now come full circle on the web development arc. Over the last five episodes, we went from \

FastAPI to a production-deployed, database-backed, authenticated API with proper logging and monitoring. That's not a tutorial toy — that's a real stack you could ship.

But here's the bigger picture: everything we've built — APIs, databases, authentication, deployment — is _infrastructure_. It moves data, stores data, protects data. The question we haven't answered yet is: what do you actually _do_ with all that data once you have it?

title.body: Trading\n\nTrading is the activity of buying and selling goods, services, or financial assets in order to make a profit. It has been an important part of human society for centuries, helping people exchange products that they need but cannot produce themselves. In the modern world, trading takes place in many forms, including local markets, international business, and online financial markets. People trade items such as food, clothes, electronics, and even digital assets. Financial trading involves buying and selling stocks, currencies, commodities, or cryptocurrencies with the aim of earning money from price changes. Traders study market trends, demand and supply, and economic news to make smart decisions. Successful trading requires knowledge, patience, and good risk management because prices can rise and fall quickly. Technology has made trading faster and more accessible through online platforms, allowing people to trade from their computers or smartphones. However, trading also involves risks, and beginners must learn carefully before investing money. Education, practice, and experience help traders improve their strategies and avoid big losses. Trading also plays an important role in the global economy because it connects producers and consumers from different parts of the world. Countries trade goods with each other to obtain resources they lack and to strengthen economic growth. Overall, trading is a powerful economic activity that supports business development, creates opportunities for profit, and helps markets function efficiently in both local and international economies.
